description:
Do you know the tall tale of Johnny Appleseed? Follow along with this folktale about John Chapman in this reading.

If you've found a new favorite I encourage you to get a copy of your own, either through purchase or from the library, to read with your favorite people again and again! If you're looking to enhance the reading material, be sure to check out the Five Bookroot Readings suggested questions below. 

#kidsbooks #kidsbooksreadaloud #ReadAloud

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Bookroot Readings suggested questions to help dive into this book. 

1. What is a folktale?  
     - A folktale is a story that is passed on orally from one teller to another. As each person tells the tale, the wording gets changed slightly; some aspects of the story can be enhanced, omitted or changed completely. Play the telephone game to place emphasis on the concept of how the message changes from the original teller to the last listener.

2. What parts of this telling of Johnny Appleseed do you think were embellished? 

3. What did Johnny Appleseed do well? 

4. Where did this story take place? Grab a map and chart out his journey. 

5. Tell me the tale of Jonny Appleseed as if I've never heard it before, and/or variations of this question:
     - Tell me how do you think this story originally happened? 
     - Retell this tale as if it were happening in modern times/today.

description:
Children's Bedtime Fairytale Stories Compilation - The Snow Queen - Little Bear Learns How.

The Snow Queen

Once upon a time there was a wicked sprite, indeed he was the most mischievous of all sprites. One day he was in a very good humor, for he had made a mirror with the power of causing all that was good and beautiful when it was reflected therein, to look poor and mean; but that which was good-for-nothing and looked ugly was shown magnified and increased in ugliness. In this mirror the most beautiful landscapes looked like boiled spinach, and the best persons were turned into frights, or appeared to stand on their heads; their faces were so distorted that they were not to be recognised; and if anyone had a mole, you might be sure that it would be magnified and spread over both nose and mouth.

"That's glorious fun!" said the sprite. If a good thought passed through a man's mind, then a grin was seen in the mirror, and the sprite laughed heartily at his clever discovery. All the little sprites who went to his school--for he kept a sprite school--told each other that a miracle had happened; and that now only, as they thought, it would be possible to see how the world really looked. They ran about with the mirror; and at last there was not a land or a person who was not represented distorted in the mirror. So then they thought they would fly up to the sky, and have a joke there. The higher they flew with the mirror, the more terribly it grinned: they could hardly hold it fast. Higher and higher still they flew, nearer and nearer to the stars, when suddenly the mirror shook so terribly with grinning, that it flew out of their hands and fell to the earth, where it was dashed in a hundred million and more pieces. And now it worked much more evil than before; for some of these pieces were hardly so large as a grain of sand, and they flew about in the wide world, and when they got into people's eyes, there they stayed; and then people saw everything perverted, or only had an eye for that which was evil. This happened because the very smallest bit had the same power which the whole mirror had possessed. Some persons even got a splinter in their heart, and then it made one shudder, for their heart became like a lump of ice. Some of the broken pieces were so large that they were used for windowpanes, through which one could not see one's friends. Other pieces were put in spectacles; and that was a sad affair when people put on their glasses to see well and rightly. Then the wicked sprite laughed till he almost choked, for all this tickled his fancy. The fine splinters still flew about in the air: and now we shall hear what happened next.

Little Bear.

This story is about Little Bear and his adventures in and around the home. Little Bear's adventures include finding the perfect cold-weather outfit to wear, making Birthday Soup for his friends, pretending to explore the moon, and listening to a bedtime story. video_title: Penguin: 6 Books for Kids Read-Aloud #pictures #story #books #learning #reading #penguin #education
description:
Penguins are fascinating flightless birds that are highly adapted to life in the water. Here’s everything you need to know about them:

1. General Facts
Scientific Order: Sphenisciformes

Family: Spheniscidae

Number of Species: 18 (debated, as some subspecies may be separate species)

Lifespan: 15–20 years (varies by species; some live longer in captivity)

Habitat: Primarily the Southern Hemisphere (Antarctica, South America, Africa, Australia, New Zealand, and nearby islands)

2. Physical Characteristics
Size: Ranges from the Little Blue Penguin (16–18 inches tall) to the Emperor Penguin (up to 4 feet tall).

Weight: 2–90 lbs (1–40 kg), depending on the species.

Coloration: Countershaded (black back, white belly) for camouflage in water.

Adaptations:

Flippers: Modified wings for swimming (can reach speeds of 15–25 mph underwater).

Dense Bones: Help them dive deep (Emperor penguins can dive over 1,800 feet!).

Waterproof Feathers: Coated with oil to stay dry and insulated.

Blubber Layer: Helps retain heat in freezing temperatures.

3. Behavior & Diet
Social Animals: Most species live in large colonies (some with thousands of penguins).

Communication: Use vocal calls and body movements to identify mates and chicks.

Diet: Mainly fish, squid, krill, and crustaceans.

Predators: Leopard seals, orcas, sharks, and seabirds (for eggs/chicks).

4. Reproduction & Parenting
Mating: Most are monogamous for a season (some for life).

Egg Laying: 1–2 eggs per breeding season (Emperor penguins lay just one).

Incubation: Males often guard the egg while females hunt (e.g., Emperor penguin males balance the egg on their feet for months).

Chicks: Hatch covered in fluffy down; parents take turns feeding them.

5. Cool Penguin Facts
Fast Swimmers: Gentoo penguins can reach 22 mph (36 km/h).

Longest Underwater Dive: Emperor penguins can stay submerged for over 20 minutes.

No Land Predators in Antarctica: Only fear predators in the water.

"Tobogganing": Slide on their bellies to move faster on ice.

Salt Glands: Excrete excess salt from seawater through their beaks.

6. Conservation Status
Threats: Climate change, overfishing, oil spills, and habitat destruction.

Endangered Species:

Galápagos Penguin (critically endangered)

Yellow-eyed Penguin (endangered)

African Penguin (endangered)

7. Popular Penguin Species
Species Location Key Trait
Emperor Penguin Antarctica Largest, breeds in harsh winter
King Penguin Sub-Antarctic islands Bright orange cheek patches
Adelie Penguin Antarctica Classic "tuxedo" look
Gentoo Penguin Sub-Antarctic Red-orange beak, fastest swimmer
Little Blue Penguin Australia/NZ Smallest penguin (also called Fairy Penguin)
8. Cultural Impact
Featured in movies like Happy Feet, March of the Penguins, and Madagascar.
Symbol of resilience due to their survival in extreme conditions.

video_title: Bees Are Our Friends (lesson about ecology/conservation) #educational  #toddlers #kindergarten #kids
description:
"Bees are our Friends" is a charming and educational children's picture book by author Toni D'Alia and illustrator Alice Lindstrom.

Here is a detailed overview of the book:

"Bees are our Friends" by Toni D'Alia & Alice Lindstrom
Genre: Children's Picture Book (Non-Fiction/Fiction blend)
Target Age Range: Typically 3-7 years old

Synopsis and Content
The book serves as a perfect, gentle introduction to the world of bees for young children. It follows a young child’s perspective as they discover the importance of bees in their garden and the wider world.

The narrative is simple and reassuring. It explains that bees are not something to be feared but are, in fact, essential friends. The book covers key concepts in a way a small child can understand:

Pollination: It shows how bees help flowers, fruits, and vegetables grow by moving pollen from one bloom to another.

Bee Products: It touches on how bees make honey.

Bee Habitat: It introduces where bees live (hives).

Coexistence: It encourages a calm and respectful attitude towards bees, explaining that they will not sting unless they feel threatened.

The central message is one of environmental stewardship and appreciation for these crucial pollinators, teaching children that protecting bees is important for our planet.

Artwork and Illustration
Alice Lindstrom's illustrations are a major highlight of the book. They are created using a unique and beautiful collage technique:

Mixed Media: The art combines painting and paper collage, giving the images a wonderful texture, depth, and a slightly retro, folk-art feel.

Color Palette: The colors are warm, sunny, and vibrant, filled with yellows, oranges, blues, and greens, perfectly evoking a sunny garden environment.

Composition: The illustrations are bold and clear, making them very engaging for young readers. The bees and flowers are depicted in a stylish yet easily recognizable way.

The artwork doesn't just support the text; it brings the garden and the bees to life, creating a joyful and inviting atmosphere.

Why It's a Beloved Book
Educational Value: It seamlessly introduces basic entomology and environmental science in an accessible, non-scary way.

Positive Message: It promotes curiosity, kindness towards nature, and dispels common fears about bees.

Artistic Merit: The stunning collage illustrations make it a visual treat for both children and adults.

Engaging for Young Readers: The text is rhythmic, simple, and repetitive in places, which is perfect for reading aloud and for early readers.

Springboard for Discussion: It encourages further conversation about gardens, insects, and how children can help bees (e.g., by planting bee-friendly flowers).

Themes
Nature and Environment: An appreciation for the natural world.

Friendship and Coexistence: Understanding how humans and nature can live together harmoniously.

Curiosity and Learning: Encouraging children to observe and learn about the world around them.

Conservation: Gently introduces the idea that small creatures play a big role and need our protection.

In summary, "Bees are our Friends" is a beautifully illustrated, thoughtfully written book that successfully combines a sweet story with an important lesson about ecology. It's a favorite among parents, teachers, and librarians for its ability to captivate young audiences while fostering a love and respect for nature.

From the creator of The Very Hungry Caterpillar comes a brilliant new Eric Carle board book for the artist in us all.
   Every child has an artist inside them, and this vibrant picture book from Eric Carle will help let it out. The artist in this book paints the world as he sees it, just like a child. There's a red crocodile, an orange elephant, a purple fox and a polka-dotted donkey. More than anything, there's imagination. Filled with some of the most magnificently colorful animals of Eric Carle's career, this book is a tribute to the creative life and celebrates the power of art.

video_title: Doggy Jitters | Read Aloud by Reading Pioneers Academy
description:
Doggy Jitters is written in fun poetic language and introduces the reader to sounds and situations that might make our pets anxious or scared. What do many dogs do when they hear the rain beat down on the roof or the thunder flash in the sky? Find out how one little dog handles her fears, and how you can help your dog overcome her fears.

Dogs have a keen sense of hearing. This means they can hear sounds that humans can't even hear.
Sometimes dogs are very sensitive to certain sounds and become nervous or anxious.
Paying attention to the noises around you might help identify what makes your pet fearful.
Help your pet avoid these triggers and comfort him or her when they happen.
Talk to your veterinarian to discover what you can do to help your pet overcome the jitters!

🎨 Visual and Literary Style
•  Khoa Le’s illustrations are lush, dreamy, and slightly spooky, perfectly complementing the lyrical text and the contrast between light and dark.

🧡 Why It Resonates
•  This book is especially meaningful for children who feel “different” or misunderstood, offering reassurance that being unique is something to be celebrated.

video_title: How to Get Your Teacher Ready (from the perspective of the students)#toddlers #kindergarten #stories
description:
How to Get Your Teacher Ready is a delightful children's picture book written by Jean Reagan and illustrated by Lee Wildish. It's part of the bestselling "How To..." series that includes How to Babysit a Grandpa and How to Catch a Santa Claus.

Here is a comprehensive guide to the book, covering its summary, themes, and why it's so popular.

Summary
The story flips the traditional dynamic on its first day of school. Instead of a teacher preparing the students, the book is a humorous and heartfelt guide where a class of diverse, enthusiastic students takes on the responsibility of preparing their teacher for the big year ahead.

Told from the perspective of the students, the book walks through the key events of the school year, offering step-by-step instructions on how to help their teacher navigate each one. The advice is a charming mix of the practical and the wildly imaginative, perfectly capturing a child's perspective.

The book is structured around these major school milestones:

The First Day of School: Students advise on how to help the teacher learn everyone's names, show them where the bathroom is, and what to do if they get lost on the way to the cafeteria.

Picture Day: They give tips on how to make sure the teacher's hair looks just right and that they don't have any broccoli in their teeth.

The 100th Day of School: The class helps the teacher find 100 things to bring for the celebration.

Field Day: They coach their teacher on how to compete in races and, most importantly, be a good sport.

Teacher Appreciation Day: The students show how to properly celebrate and thank their teacher.

The Last Day of School: They help the teacher cope with saying goodbye and getting ready for summer vacation.

Throughout the book, the children are portrayed as confident, kind, and capable leaders, while the teacher is shown as slightly nervous but eager and loving, following the students' guidance with trust and appreciation.

Key Themes
Role Reversal: The core charm of the book comes from the kids being the knowledgeable experts. This is empowering for young readers and very funny for adults.

Empathy and Caring: The underlying message is about kindness, helping others, and building a supportive community. The students care for their teacher's emotional and practical needs.

School Community: It beautifully depicts the classroom as a family where everyone looks out for one another.

Anticipating and Navigating New Experiences: The book provides a gentle, humorous roadmap for common school-year events, which can help ease children's anxieties about them.

Why It's So Popular (And Why Kids and Parents Love It)
Relatability: Every child who has ever started a new school year will see themselves in this story.

Humor: The illustrations and the premise are genuinely funny. The idea of a teacher needing help to find the bathroom or remember names is hilarious to kids.

Empowerment: It gives children a sense of control and confidence. It shows them that they have important knowledge and can be helpers.

Wonderful Illustrations: Lee Wildish's artwork is vibrant, detailed, and full of little jokes. Children love spending time on each page discovering all the funny things happening in the classroom.

Great Read-Aloud: The instructional, guidebook style makes it engaging and interactive to read aloud.

About the Author: Jean Reagan
Jean Reagan was born in Alabama but spent most of her childhood in Colorado. She didn't start writing books until later in life, after careers in teaching and park ranging, and raising her children. Her "How To" series was inspired by her own grandchildren. The first book, How to Babysit a Grandpa, was an instant success and launched her career as a beloved children's author.

Other books in the series include:

How to Babysit a Grandma

How to Raise a Mom

How to Surprise a Dad

How to Catch a Santa Claus

How to Get Your Elf Ready

How to Welcome a New Baby

In essence, How to Get Your Teacher Ready is more than just a back-to-school book. It's a year-round celebration of the special bond between students and their teacher, filled with humor, heart, and a powerful message about empathy and community.

video_title: My Heart and Mind: A Children's Book About Learning Emotions and Feelings Read Aloud
description:
My Heart and Mind is a story of Marshal, a kid who is growing and with this growth, he is facing the challenge of managing his feelings and emotions. Understanding emotions and helping kids to help themselves is crucial for parents and teachers to make them able to know, understand and manage their emotions.

Social-emotional learning at the developing stage of a child’s mind is very important. Parents and Teachers have all the responsibility to help kids in learning through social-emotional books which include their favorite characters like Marshal who feel the same as they feel.

We can’t deny that Emotions are the most important aspect of our humanity and my goal is to have children feel comfortable with all of their emotions by seeing their favorite characters like Marshal. This will improve their emotional intelligence and hopefully make them more open to conversations about how things make them feel.

A Colorful picture and Rhyming storybook “My Heart and Mind: A Children’s Book Learning about Feelings and Emotions” the first book from the series “Unlocking the Gold-mine Minds”has been found to be a great help for parenting a child with intense emotions and a perfect teacher and therapists toolbox.

description:
Dr. Seuss, also known as Theodor Seuss Geisel, was an American writer and illustrator celebrated for his whimsical and imaginative children’s books. His works are characterized by playful rhymes, nonsense words, and delightful creatures.
 Let’s explore some of his most iconic books:
“The Cat in the Hat”: Written in 1957, this classic features a tall, anthropomorphic cat with a red and white-striped top hat. The Cat’s mischievous antics ensue when he visits Sally and her brother on a rainy day while their mother is away.
“Green Eggs and Ham”: In this delightful tale, Sam-I-Am persistently tries to convince a skeptical character to try green eggs and ham. The repetitive rhymes make it a favorite for young readers.
“How the Grinch Stole Christmas!”: A heartwarming holiday story about the Grinch, who learns the true meaning of Christmas. His heart grows three sizes as he discovers the joy of giving.
“Horton Hears a Who!”: Horton the elephant hears a tiny voice coming from a speck of dust. He vows to protect the Whos living on that speck, emphasizing the importance of kindness and empathy.
“The Lorax”: An environmental fable that encourages readers to care for the planet. The Lorax speaks for the trees and warns against greed and destruction.
“Oh, the Places You’ll Go!”: A motivational book that celebrates life’s journey, filled with ups and downs. Dr. Seuss inspires readers to embrace adventure and overcome challenges.
Remember, Dr. Seuss’s books aren’t just for kids; they resonate with readers of all ages, reminding us to embrace imagination, kindness, and the joy of storytelling.

Zachary uses his creativity and knowledge of geometry to tackle the project. Throughout the story, he learns about various geometric concepts such as area, perimeter, and dimensions, and how these can be applied to transform shapes in innovative ways.

Zachary's journey demonstrates that math can be both fun and useful, inspiring readers to think outside the box and apply their knowledge in creative ways.

The key lesson of the book is that math is not just about numbers and formulas; it's about thinking critically and solving problems. Zachary's adventures show that with a little creativity and a solid understanding of basic math principles, anyone can become a "shape transformer." The book also encourages children to embrace challenges and view them as opportunities to learn and grow.

description:
Have you ever wondered how bread is made? Follow along with this short storytime to learn about how a wheat seed becomes a loaf of bread! 

If you've found a new favorite I encourage you to get a copy of your own, either through purchase or from the library, to read with your favorite people again and again! Additionally, if you're looking to enhance the reading material, be sure to check out the Five Bookroot Readings suggested questions below. 

0:00 - Introduction
0:37 - A farmer plants wheat.
0:53 - The farmer cuts the wheat.
1:13 - Machines make flour.
1:37 - The flour is bagged.
2:00 - A baker makes dough.
2:18 - A mixer stirs the dough.
2:33 - The dough rises.
2:48 - The baker shapes loaves.
3:00 - The loaves are baked. 
3:16 - Time to eat!
3:30 - Glossary

#kidsbooks #kidsbooksreadaloud #ReadAloud
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Bookroot Readings suggested questions to help dive into this book. 

1. Have you ever thought about the process of how bread is made? We often grab a loaf from the grocery store and don't give a thought to how it got there. What is the first step that must be done for the production of that loaf of bread? (0:37)

2. After the wheat is planted, grown, harvested, ground into flour, then bagged; what is the next step in turning the wheat into bread? (2:00)

3. One important step this book did not touch on, is distribution. How did the freshly baked loaf of bread get to the grocery store? 

4. There are lots of steps from wheat to bread. How many different companies/people do you think does it take to make a loaf? 

5. Next time you purchase a loaf of wheat, (or make your own with your favorite people!) think back to this reading and say thanks to all the people who ultimately made that loaf possible.

description:

description:
"Little Blue Truck's Springtime" is a beloved children's book. Here is a detailed overview, perfect for a parent, educator, or curious reader.

Overview of "Little Blue Truck's Springtime"
"Little Blue Truck's Springtime" is a delightful board book written by Alice Schertle and illustrated by Jill McElmurry. It is part of the hugely popular Little Blue Truck series.

This book is specifically designed for very young readers (toddlers and preschoolers) to celebrate the joy and renewal of the spring season.

At a Glance
Author: Alice Schertle

Illustrator: Jill McElmurry

Publisher: Houghton Mifflin Harcourt

Target Age: 1-4 years old

Format: Board book (sturdy pages perfect for little hands)

Key Features: Rhyming text, animal sounds, lift-the-flap elements, a cheerful spring theme.

The Story (Plot Summary)
The story follows the friendly Little Blue Truck and his pal Toad as they take a joyful drive through the countryside on a bright spring day.

As they drive along, Blue and Toad greet all their animal friends who are enjoying the beautiful weather and the new life that spring has brought. The narrative is built around a simple, engaging question: "Who's peeking out? Guess who!"

Each spread features a different animal parent with their baby (or babies). The reader is encouraged to lift the flap to reveal the adorable baby animal hiding behind a bush, in a nest, or under a log.

The book concludes with a sweet and humorous twist: after meeting all the new babies, Little Blue Truck himself gets a surprise "hello" from his own very special "baby."

Key Themes and Things to Look For:
The Magic of Spring: The book is a pure celebration of spring. The illustrations are bursting with pastel colors, blooming flowers, green grass, and bright sunshine, perfectly capturing the season's feeling of warmth and new beginnings.

Animal Babies and Names: A primary educational element is teaching the names of baby animals. It's a fantastic way for toddlers to learn that a baby sheep is a lamb, a baby horse is a foal, a baby duck is a duckling, etc.

Friendship and Community: True to the series' spirit, the book emphasizes friendly greetings ("Beep! Beep! Beep!") and the joy of connecting with neighbors and friends.

Interactive Lift-the-Flaps: The flaps are the main interactive feature. They encourage fine motor skills, curiosity, and prediction. The question "Guess who!" turns reading into a fun game.

Rhythm and Rhyme: Alice Schertle's signature rhyming text is melodic and easy to read aloud. The rhythm is bouncy and engaging, making it a perfect read-aloud book that children will quickly memorize.

Beautiful Illustrations: Jill McElmurry's artwork is charming and detailed. The pages are filled with cheerful, vintage-style illustrations that feel both classic and fresh. Children love looking at the tiny bugs, blooming flowers, and expressive animal faces.

Why Kids and Parents Love It:
Familiar Characters: Children who know Little Blue Truck from other books are immediately comforted and excited to see him again.

Perfect for Easter: It's a very popular non-religious Easter gift, often found in Easter baskets alongside books like "The Tale of Peter Rabbit."

Engaging and Educational: It seamlessly combines a fun story with learning about nature and seasons.

Positive and Uplifting: The book is full of cheer, kindness, and the simple joys of a beautiful day.

The Little Blue Truck Series
This book is a spin-off from the original series. If your child loves it, they will likely enjoy:

Little Blue Truck (the original)

Little Blue Truck Leads the Way

Little Blue Truck's Halloween

Little Blue Truck's Christmas

Good Night, Little Blue Truck

In summary, "Little Blue Truck's Springtime" is a vibrant, interactive, and heartwarming board book that perfectly captures the excitement of spring and the delight of meeting new baby animals. It's a seasonal favorite that families return to year after year.

description:
"Bee" by Britta Teekentrup is a beloved and critically acclaimed children's picture book. Here's a detailed overview of the book.

Overview
"Bee" is a beautifully illustrated, rhyming picture book that follows the journey of a single bee as it pollinates a variety of flowers. Published in 2017, it is part of a larger series by Teekentrup that explores nature and the environment, including other titles like "Tree," "Moon," and "Ocean."

The book is renowned for its peek-through pages, where a cut-out in the shape of a bee travels from page to page, creating a dynamic and interactive reading experience.

Key Features
Peek-Through Illustrations: This is the book's most distinctive feature. A die-cut hole representing the bee appears on every page, guiding the reader through the story. As the pages turn, the hole moves through different vibrant landscapes, always maintaining the bee's presence in the narrative.

Lyrical Rhyming Text: The text is simple, rhythmic, and poetic, making it perfect for reading aloud to young children. The rhyme scheme is engaging and helps to convey the importance and wonder of the bee's work in an accessible way.

Example from the text:

"We are linked to the bees, / From the birds in the sky / To the fish in the seas, / To the flowers and the trees."

Educational & Environmental Message: While primarily a story, the book gently introduces young readers to the concept of pollination and underscores the critical role bees play in our ecosystem. It delivers a powerful message about the interconnectedness of nature and the importance of protecting bees without being heavy-handed.

Stunning Artwork: Britta Teekentrup's art style is instantly recognizable. For "Bee," she uses a palette of warm yellows, oranges, greens, and blues, creating a collage-like effect that is both modern and timeless. The illustrations are lush, textured, and full of detail for children to explore.

Themes
The Importance of Bees: The book is a celebration of bees and their vital work as pollinators.

Interconnectedness: It shows how one small creature is connected to the entire natural world.

Nature's Cycle: The story beautifully depicts the cycle of life and growth in a garden or meadow.

Conservation: It subtly encourages care and respect for the environment and its creatures.

Target Audience
The book is ideally suited for:

Toddlers and Preschoolers (Ages 2-5)

Early readers due to its simple, rhythmic text.

Parents and educators looking for books that combine beautiful art with a meaningful message about nature.

Why It's So Popular
"Bee" succeeds because it masterfully combines several elements:

Interactive Design: The peek-through hole is irresistible to little hands and eyes.

Read-Aloud Appeal: The rhyme and rhythm make it a joy to read repeatedly.

Visual Beauty: It's a truly gorgeous book that appeals to both children and adults.

Timely Message: Its environmental theme is highly relevant, making it a book that feels both enjoyable and important.

In summary, Britta Teekentrup's "Bee" is more than just a picture book; it's an immersive and educational experience. It captures the magic of nature through its innovative design and powerful, simple poetry, leaving a lasting impression on its readers about the significance of these small but mighty insects.

Spork sticks out. In his kitchen, utensils have a single purpose. Even though he tries to act more spoonish or look more forkish, he never gets picked at mealtime. Instead, he sits and watches while the forks twirl knots of noodles and the spoons scoop up mountains of peas. They even get to enjoy a bubbly bath in the sink when dinner is over.

He seems destined for a life in the drawer … until one day, a messy guest arrives. This guest doesn’t seem to care about cutlery customs. Spork wonders—could this be his chance to find his way to the table? Could his uniqueness make him the best solution for this problem?

A metaphor-rich celebration of hybrid identities, Spork is a “multi-cutlery” tale for anyone who’s ever felt like a misfit. Exploring themes of purpose, conformity, diversity, and finding your place in the world, Spork is written by Kyo Maclear and illustrated by Isabelle Arsenault. Published by Kids Can Press.

description:
Let's talk about consent! Based on the research that consent should be discussed with toddlers on up, this book offers adults the opportunity to begin important conversations with young children in an informed, safe, and supported way. Get the book: https://bit.ly/3JC4Duu

For more children's book recommendations and tips for raising kids who love to read, visit Brightly: http://bit.ly/299HQX0

ABOUT YES! NO!: A FIRST CONVERSATION ABOUT CONSENT

Developed by experts in the fields of early childhood development and activism against injustice, this topic-driven book offers clear, concrete language and imagery to introduce the concept of consent. YES! NO! serves to normalize and celebrate the experience of asking for and being asked for permission to do something involving one's body. It centers on respect for bodily autonomy, and reviews the many ways that one can say or indicate "No."

While young children are avid observers and questioners of their world, but sometimes it's hard to know where to begin when talking about complicated topics. Research shows that discussing issues like race, gender, and our bodies early helps children understand what they see, also increases self-awareness, self-esteem, and allows them to recognize and confront things that are unfair, like discrimination and prejudice.

description:
“Skeleton for Dinner” by Margery Cuyler is a humorous Halloween-themed picture book that teaches kids about misunderstandings, friendship, and communication.

In Skeleton for Dinner, Big Witch and Little Witch brew a delicious stew and decide to invite their spooky friends—Ghost, Ghoul, and Skeleton—for dinner. They write the guest list and pin it to a tree. But Skeleton stumbles upon the list and misinterprets it: he thinks the witches want to eat him and his friends for dinner!
Panicked, Skeleton, Ghost, and Ghoul flee into the woods to hide. When Little Witch goes to find them, they’re nowhere to be seen. Thankfully, Crow spots the list and realizes the mix-up. description:
Take Away the A by Michaël Escoffier, illustrated by Kris Di Giacomo. Read by Riko.

Take Away the A is a fun, imaginative romp through the alphabet. The idea behind the book is that within every language there are words that change and become a different word through the simple subtraction of a single letter. In other words, without the "A," the Beast is Best. Or, without the "M," a chomp becomes a chop—though it could be that this particular play on words didn't even make it into the book, there are so many! We certainly don't want to give too much away. . . . Now, take a look and find some more! Discovering all of the words in the book is a lot of fun, and then there's the wild, exciting adventure that follows, of trying to find more!

Do you want to teach your children how to be grateful for the things they already have?
Little Betsy will learn that happiness is made up of simple things in life, both small and big. With the help of the magic stone, she will begin to feel gratitude for her parents, friends, and toys. This book will help your kids in many ways:

About BRAVE

Each morning, Dad brushes the knots from his son’s long hair to braid it. The boy winces at the tugging, and at school he’s teased for his braid. But he remembers the stories of how his father and grandpa were forced to cut their hair and forbidden from practicing their traditions when they were young, and how they fought to make it possible for him to wear his hair long. Although it can hurt, having long hair ultimately makes him feel brave and strong.

This powerful picture book by author-illustrator Weshoyot Alvitre examines the traumatic history of colonization and reclaims Native pride in long hair, delivering a tender father-son story that’s perfect for fans of Hair Love and Love in the Library.

description:
Steam Train, Dream Train is a delightful picture book that chugs into the hearts of young readers. Written by Sherri Duskey Rinker and illustrated by Tom Lichtenheld, this whimsical tale takes us on a dreamy train ride filled with animal workers, cargo, and bedtime magic:

Polar bears pack the reefer car with ice cream.
Elephants fill the tanker cars with paints.
Tortoises stock the auto rack with race cars.
Bouncy kangaroos stuff the hopper car with balls.
As the train gets ready for its nocturnal journey, it’s a symphony of sweet, silly dreams and happy smiles. Whether your little one is a budding train enthusiast or simply loves imaginative stories, this book is perfect for:

Read-aloud moments: Share the rhythmic text with your child.
Early readers: The simple words make it great for kids beginning to read on their own.
Animal lovers: Introduce your child to new animals and their quirky roles on the dream train.

Awdry and illustrated by Robin Davies, this interactive lift-the-flap adventure takes us on a journey with Thomas and his friends as they discover the ever-changing weather conditions:

“What’s the weather today, Thomas?”
Lift the flaps to find out!

Thomas

Sir Topham Hatt

video_title: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom - Read Along Story book - Digital HD - Harrison Ford, Spielberg
description:
Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom, Read Along Story book. Eminent archaeologist Indiana Jones is back in his second adventure, this time to tackle the great terror surrounding the mysterious Temple of Doom. After crash landing in India, Indiana Jones and companions Short Round and Willie Scott end up in a small distressed village where the residents claim a dark power has stolen their precious stone... and their children! Agreeing to assist the village, Indiana and friends make their way to a nearby palace and inquire further into the strange happenings. Assuring Indiana he has no idea what he's talking about, prime minister Chatter Lal offers them to spend the night in the palace. However, it is that evening that Indiana discovers a secret passage into a booby-trapped temple and stumbles onto something he thought was long extinct. It seems the age old cut of Thuggee cult is attempting to rise once more, believing that with the power of the five Sankara stones they can rule the world. Now, it's up to Indiana to put a stop to the Thuggee campaign, rescue the lost children, win the girl and conquer the Temple of Doom. 

Cast of the full movie version included...

►Harrison Ford as Indiana Jones: An archaeologist adventurer who is asked by a desperate Indian village to retrieve a mysterious stone and rescue the missing village children. Ford undertook a strict physical exercise regimen headed by Jake Steinfeld to gain a more muscular tone for the part.

►Kate Capshaw as Wilhelmina "Willie" Scott: An American nightclub singer working in Shanghai. Willie is unprepared for her adventure with Indy and Short Round, and appears to be a damsel in distress. She also forms a romantic relationship with Indy. Over 120 actresses auditioned for the role, including Sharon Stone. To prepare for the role, Capshaw watched The African Queen and A Guy Named Joe. Spielberg wanted Willie to be a complete contrast to Marion Ravenwood from Raiders of the Lost Ark, so Capshaw dyed her brown hair blonde for the part. Costume designer Anthony Powell wanted the character to have red hair.

►Amrish Puri as Mola Ram: A Thuggee priest who performs rituals of human sacrifices. The character is named after a 17th-century Indian painter. Lucas wanted Mola Ram to be terrifying, so the screenwriters added elements of Aztec and Hawaiian human sacrificers, and European devil worship to the character. To create his headdress, make-up artist Tom Smith based the skull on a cow (as this would be sacrilegious), and used a latex shrunken head.

►Jonathan Ke Quan as Short Round: Indy's eleven-year-old Chinese sidekick, who drives the 1936 Auburn Boat Tail Speedster which allows Indy to escape during the opening sequence. Quan was chosen as part of a casting call in Los Angeles. Around 6000 actors auditioned worldwide for the part: Quan was cast after his brother auditioned for the role. Spielberg liked his personality, so he and Ford improvised the scene where Short Round accuses Indy of cheating during a card game. He was credited by his birthname, Ke Huy Quan.

►Roshan Seth as Chattar Lal: The Prime Minister of the Maharaja of Pankot. Chattar, also a Thuggee worshiper, is enchanted by Indy, Willie and Short Round's arrival, but is offended by Indy's questioning of the palace's history and the archaeologist's own dubious past.

►Philip Stone as Captain Philip Blumburtt: A British Indian Army Captain called to Pankot Palace for "exercises". Alongside a unit of his riflemen, Blumburtt assists Indy towards the end in fighting off Thuggee reinforcements. David Niven was attached to the role but died before filming began.

►Roy Chiao as Lao Che: A Shanghai crime boss who, with his sons, hires Indy to recover the cremated ashes of one of his ancestors, only to attempt to kill him and cheat him out of his fee, a large diamond.

►David Yip as Wu Han: A friend of Indy. He is killed by one of Lao Che's sons while posing as a waiter at Club Obi Wan.

►Raj Singh as Zalim Singh, the adolescent Maharajá of Pankot, who appears as an innocent puppet of the Thuggee faithful. In the end, he helps to defeat them.

►D. R. Nanayakkara as Shaman: The leader of a small village that recruits Indy to retrieve their stolen sacred Shiva lingam stone.

► Director: Steven Spielberg
► Writers: Willard Huyck (screenplay), Gloria Katz (screenplay)

video_title: The Construction Alphabet Book | The Children Who Loved Books | Kids Picture Book-Read Aloud
description:
“The Construction Alphabet Book” by Jerry Pallotta is an engaging and noisy alphabet book that explores construction equipment from A to Z. Let’s dive into the world of construction machines and discover fascinating details:

A is for Asphalt Roller: This heavy roller smooths out freshly laid asphalt.
B is for Bulldozer: A powerful machine that pushes dirt and debris.
C is for Cement Mixer: It blends sand, gravel, and water to create concrete.
D is for Dump Truck: These trucks transport dirt, rocks, and other materials.
E is for Excavator: With its hydraulic arm, it digs deep into the ground.
F is for Front-End Loader: It scoops up dirt and moves it around.
G is for Grader: Used to level the ground and create smooth surfaces.
H is for Hammer: The mighty jackhammer breaks through tough surfaces.
I is for I-Beam: These steel beams provide structural support.
J is for Jackhammer: Another nod to this powerful tool.
K is for Knuckleboom Crane: It lifts and moves heavy objects.
L is for Ladder Truck: Firefighters use these to reach high places.

video_title: Mister Seahorse (celebrate the special role of a father figure) #educational #toddlers #kindergarten
description:
Mister Seahorse is a beloved children's book by the iconic author and illustrator Eric Carle. Here is a detailed overview perfect for parents, teachers, or curious readers.

Overview of Mister Seahorse by Eric Carle
Author & Illustrator: Eric Carle
First Published: 2004
Target Age Range: 3-7 years old
Themes: Fatherhood, underwater life, nature, caregiving, camouflage.

The Story in a Nutshell
The book follows Mister Seahorse as he swims through the ocean after Mrs. Seahorse has laid her eggs in his pouch. He is carrying their future babies and feeling very proud and careful. As he journeys, he meets several other fish fathers who are also caring for their eggs and babies in various ways.

The unique and magical twist of the book is Eric Carle's classic collage art. Many pages have "see-through" clear acetate pages printed with seaweed, rocks, or coral that act as camouflage. When you turn these transparent pages, you reveal the hidden fish fathers, making reading an interactive and discovery-filled experience.

Meet the Fish Dads Mister Seahorse Encounters
A key part of the book's charm is introducing children to the real-life phenomenon of male parenting in the animal kingdom. Mister Seahorse meets:

Mr. Stickleback: Guards the eggs his mate laid in a nest.

Mr. Tilapia: Holds the eggs in his mouth to keep them safe (a process called mouthbrooding).

Mr. Kurtus: (The Nurseryfish) Has eggs stuck to his head.

Mr. Pipe: Carries eggs on his belly, similar to a seahorse.

Mr. Bullhead: Guards his eggs in a rocky crevice.

Each interaction is gentle and reassuring, with Mister Seahorse offering a kind "Good luck, then!" as he continues on his way.

Key Themes and What Children Learn
Active Fatherhood: The book beautifully challenges traditional gender roles in parenting by showcasing fathers as primary, nurturing caregivers. It's a wonderful story for dads to read to their children.

Marine Biology: It introduces kids to a variety of underwater creatures and the fascinating concept of animal fathers who care for their young.

Camouflage: The clear overlay pages provide a fun, hands-on lesson in how animals use camouflage to hide from danger.

Responsibility and Care: The story emphasizes the gentle, protective nature of parenting.

Repetition and Predictability: The repetitive structure of meeting new fish is perfect for young readers, helping them anticipate what comes next.

Why Parents and Kids Love It
Stunning Artwork: Eric Carle's hand-painted tissue paper collages are vibrant, textured, and instantly recognizable.

Interactive Element: The clear acetate pages are a huge hit, making children feel like they are discovering hidden secrets on every page.

Educational Value: It seamlessly blends a sweet story with real scientific facts.

Soothing Tone: The narrative is calm, repetitive, and perfect for a bedtime story.

Celebrates Dads: It's a standout book for Father's Day or any day to celebrate the special role of a father figure.

Potential Considerations for Very Young Readers
The vocabulary can be a bit advanced for the youngest listeners (words like "transparent," "reeds," "anchored"). However, this is a great opportunity to build their language skills.

The story is more focused on a concept (animal fathers caring for young) than a high-action plot. Children who prefer very energetic stories might find it slow.

Overall Impression
Mister Seahorse is a classic Eric Carle book that combines beautiful art, innovative book design, and gentle education. It’s a heartwarming celebration of fatherhood in the animal world that continues to captivate and charm a new generation of readers. It’s a wonderful addition to any child's library.

video_title: 💬 THE INTERPRETER - Bilingual Read Aloud with the Author | Brightly Storytime
description:
Join author Olivia Abtahi for a story about a young soccer-loving girl who’s an interpreter for her Spanish-speaking parents.

Get the book: https://bit.ly/41ocpT1

About THE INTERPRETER

Some kids have one job: to be a kid! Cecilia has two. When she isn’t on the soccer field scoring goals, she’s accompanying her parents to all kinds of grown-up places, like the DMV, the accountant’s office, and the auto shop. She helps them translate from Spanish to English and from English to Spanish. It’s an important job, and it can even be fun. It’s also hard work. 

Sometimes Cecilia’s second job is so much responsibility, it feels like she’ll split in two! Is it time for Cecilia to blow her whistle and call for a time-out?

Olivia Abtahi’s clever text and Monica Arnaldo’s charming illustrations capture a common aspect of life for immigrant and bilingual families while offering a model for teamwork that helps everyone feel understood.

•  Despite some homesickness and questionable camp cuisine, Homer embraces the experience and returns home with a new sense of pride.

•  Identity & Imagination: Homer’s journey reflects the desire to explore one’s wild side and embrace new experiences.

video_title: Just Ask! - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook - NO ADS
description:
Supreme Court Justice Sonia Sotomayor and award-winning artist Rafael Lopez create a kind and caring book about the differences that make each of us unique.

Feeling different, especially as a kid, can be tough. But in the same way that different types of plants and flowers make a garden more beautiful and enjoyable, different types of people make our world more vibrant and wonderful.

In Just Ask, United States Supreme Court Justice Sonia Sotomayor celebrates the different abilities kids (and people of all ages) have. Using her own experience as a child who was diagnosed with diabetes, Justice Sotomayor writes about children with all sorts of challenges--and looks at the special powers those kids have as well. As the kids work together to build a community garden, asking questions of each other along the way, this book encourages readers to do the same: When we come across someone who is different from us but we're not sure why, all we have to do is Just Ask.

video_title: Lift And Shift: Toys That Build (Cognitive & Early Literacy Skills) #educational #toddlers #kids
description:
"Lift and Shift: Toys That Build Kids" is not a single, famous book but rather a popular and descriptive book title concept or genre within children's publishing, particularly for very young readers (ages 0-3).

Here's a detailed breakdown of what this phrase means and the kind of book it describes.

What "Lift and Shift" Means
This phrase refers to two specific types of interactive features in board books:

Lift-the-Flap: The child lifts a flap on the page to reveal a hidden picture or answer a question (e.g., "Who is behind the door?").

Shift-the-Slide (or Pull-the-Tab): The child moves a cardboard slider or tab to make something happen on the page (e.g., sliding a piece to make a rocket blast off, a dinosaur's mouth open, or a car race across the page).

The phrase "Toys That Build Kids" highlights the educational value. These books aren't just for reading; they are interactive toys designed to develop crucial early learning skills.

Common Themes and Examples of These Books
You will find countless books that fit this description, often with similar titles. They are typically sturdy, high-quality board books.

Popular Series and Titles include:

Usborne Publishing's "Peep Inside" series: Famous for intricate lift-the-flap scenes that explore nature, vehicles, and more.

"Dear Zoo" by Rod Campbell: A classic lift-the-flap book about a child receiving various animals from the zoo.

"Where's Spot?" by Eric Hill: The original lift-the-flap book about searching for a puppy.

"Busy" series (e.g., "Busy Airport," "Busy Farm"): These often combine flaps with sliders to show moving parts.

Books by Matthew Van Fleet: His books (like "Heads" or "Tails") often include pull-tabs, textures, and flaps to teach about animals.

How These Books "Build Kids" (Developmental Benefits)
The "Toy" aspect builds the child in several key areas:

1. Cognitive & Early Literacy Skills:

Cause and Effect: The child learns that their action (lifting, sliding) causes a reaction (something appears or moves). This is a fundamental cognitive concept.

Object Permanence: For the very young, lifting a flap to find something hidden reinforces that things exist even when they can't be seen.

Problem-Solving & Prediction: They learn to guess what might be under the flap or what will happen when they move the slider.

Vocabulary: These books introduce nouns (animal names, vehicle parts), verbs (lift, slide, open, close), and adjectives (colors, sizes).

2. Motor Skills:

Fine Motor Skills: The precise hand movements required to pinch, lift, and slide the tabs are excellent for developing the small muscles in the fingers and hands. This is crucial for later skills like writing.

Hand-Eye Coordination: The child must coordinate what they see with the movement of their hands to successfully manipulate the flaps and sliders.

3. Sensory Engagement:

They turn reading into a multi-sensory, hands-on experience. This is far more engaging for a toddler than a static picture and helps build a positive association with books.

4. Social & Emotional Development:

These books are perfect for shared reading. A parent and child can play and discover together, strengthening bonds.

They teach concepts like surprise and anticipation ("What will we find?!").

What to Look for When Buying These Books
If you're searching for a good "lift and shift" book, consider:

Age Appropriateness: Check the recommended age on the product. Books for under 18 months have simpler, larger flaps. Books for 2-3 year olds can have more complex mechanisms.

Durability: Look for thick, cardboard pages and well-reinforced flaps. Flaps that are taped or glued on poorly will be ripped off quickly.

Educational Content: Choose a theme that aligns with the child's interests (dinosaurs, construction vehicles, animals) to maximize engagement.

Safety: Ensure there are no small parts that could be a choking hazard for children who still mouth objects.

In summary, a "Lift and Shift: Toys That Build Kids" book is a hands-on, interactive board book designed to entertain toddlers while simultaneously building their foundational cognitive, motor, and sensory skills. It’s a perfect blend of play and learning.

description:
“The Man Who Walked Between the Towers” is a captivating children’s picture book written and illustrated by the talented American author Mordicai Gerstein. Published in 2003, this remarkable book recounts the awe-inspiring achievement of Philippe Petit, a daring Frenchman who accomplished an extraordinary feat: he walked on a tightrope wire between the roofs of the twin towers of the World Trade Center in August 19741.

The story follows Philippe Petit, a former street performer turned high-wire artist, as he becomes obsessed with the idea of walking a high-wire between the twin towers. With meticulous planning and determination, he manages to sneak into the still-under-construction towers disguised as a construction worker. Along with his friends, he carries around 440 lbs of cable through the elevator to the top floors and waits until nightfall. At midnight, they shoot an arrow across to Philippe, but due to the wind, it lands on a ledge. Philippe retrieves the arrow by crawling down the ledge and attaches a stronger line. After securing the line across the two towers, he embarks on his daring walk.

On the dawn of August 7, 1974, Philippe puts on his specially prepared black shirt and tights, picks up his 28-foot balancing pole, and steps onto the wire. As he walks, dances, and even rests on the wire, bystanders notice his incredible feat and quickly notify the police. Officers rush to the roof, yelling, “You’re under arrest!” But for almost an hour, Philippe continues to defy gravity, feeling “alone and absolutely free” in the vast expanse between the towers.

Mordicai Gerstein’s illustrations beautifully capture the poetry and magic of this historic event, earning him the prestigious 2004 Caldecott Medal12. The book has also been adapted into a film and a ballet, ensuring that Philippe Petit’s daring walk remains an enduring inspiration for generations to come.

► About Gremlins

Gremlins is a 1984 American comedy horror film directed by Joe Dante and released by Warner Bros. The film is about a young man who receives a strange creature called a mogwai as a pet, which then spawns other creatures who transform into small, destructive, evil monsters. This story was continued with a sequel, Gremlins 2: The New Batch, released in 1990. Unlike the lighter sequel, Gremlins opts for more black comedy, balanced against a Christmastime setting. Both films were the center of large merchandising campaigns.

Steven Spielberg was the film's executive producer and the screenplay was written by Chris Columbus. The film stars Zach Galligan and Phoebe Cates, with Howie Mandel providing the voice of Gizmo, the main mogwai character. Gremlins was a commercial success and received positive reviews from critics. However, the film was also heavily criticized for some of its more violent sequences. In response to this and to similar complaints about Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom, Spielberg suggested that the Motion Picture Association of America (MPAA) alter its rating system, which it did within two months of the film's release.

description:

video_title: Shimmer And Shine-Wish Upon A Sleepover@Readingtimewithnana
Tom's Great-Grandma Eileen Written By Kate Melton©
description:
“Those we love don't go away!” They always live in our hearts and die only when we forget them, breaking that invisible string. This is the main idea of this absolutely wonderful picture book. Delicate and moving, wise and fascinating, it is all about life, love, loss and the power of memories.

Death is a tricky concept and talking to children about it is never easy. This absolutely unique rhyming story helps kindergarten and school-aged children understand that death is natural and that grief and sadness are normal feelings to go through.  

The book was written in cooperation with children psychologists and even includes particular recommendations motivating parents to talk with their children about death. Soothing and beautiful illustrations, heart-warming rhymes and touching message make this children’s book an inimitable way to help your kids cope with the loss of a loved one and learn about live cycles and passing away in a sensitive and clever way.

video_title: ⏰ Over-Scheduled Andrew
description:
Over-Scheduled Andrew by Ashley Spires.

Andrew loves putting on plays so he decides to join the drama club at school. Determined to make his performance the best it can be, he joins the debate club to practice his public speaking. He signs up for dance and karate to help with his coordination. Then he's asked to play for the tennis team and edit the school newspaper. Before long he's learning to play the bagpipes, attending Spanish classes and joining the French film club. Suddenly Andrew doesn't have time for anything or anyone else, not even his best friend Edie. And he definitely doesn't have time to sleep. Will Andrew figure out how to balance all his favorite activities and his best friend at the same time? A hilarious look at over-scheduling, a common issue many kids today face.

The Living Daylights (1987) Read along book and tape, digital HD version. During a training operation, a "00" agent is unexpectedly murdered. When British agent James Bond organises the defection of a top ranking Russian general, the general divulges a plan by the bad guys to kill all its enemy agents. Bond is suspicious of the plot, but nevertheless is ordered to kill the enemy officer masterminding the operation.

► Cast of the full movie version were...

Timothy Dalton as James Bond: an MI6 agent assigned to look into the deaths of and conspiracies against several of his allies.

Maryam d'Abo as Kara Milovy: Koskov's girlfriend and later Bond's love interest.

Joe Don Baker as Brad Whitaker: An American arms dealer and self-styled general. Baker called his character "a nut" who "thought he was Napoleon".

John Rhys-Davies as General Leonid Pushkin: The new head of the enemy, replacing General Gogol.

Art Malik as Kamran Shah: a leader in the Afghan Mujahideen.

Jeroen Krabbé as General Georgi Koskov: Whitaker's ally and a renegade Russian general.

Andreas Wisniewski as Necros: Koskov's henchman, who poses repeated threats to Bond.

Thomas Wheatley as Saunders: Bond's ally.

Robert Brown as M: The head of MI6 and Bond's superior.

Desmond Llewelyn as Q: MI6's "quartermaster", who supplies Bond with multi-purpose vehicles and gadgets useful in the latter's mission.

Geoffrey Keen as Frederick Gray: The British Minister of Defence

Caroline Bliss as Miss Moneypenny: M's secretary.

John Terry as Felix Leiter: A CIA agent and ally to Bond.

Walter Gotell as General Gogol: The retired head of the enemy, now a diplomat shown in a cameo at the end of the film.

Virginia Hey as Rubavitch: General Leonid Pushkin's mistress in Morocco

Julie T. Wallace as Rosika Miklos: James Bond's contact in Bratislava, Czechoslovakia who works at the TransSiberian Pipeline.

Nadim Sawalha cameos as a police chief in Tangier. Sawalha also appeared in a previous 007 film, The Spy Who Loved Me (1977), as Aziz Fekkesh.

► Director: John Glen
► Writers: Richard Maibaum (screenplay), Michael G. Wilson (screenplay)

☆ Trivia

Originally the film was proposed to be a prequel in the series, an idea that eventually resurfaced with the reboot of the series in 2006. SMERSH, the fictionalised Russian counterintelligence agency that featured in Fleming's Casino Royale and several other early James Bond novels, was an acronym for Smiert Shpionam – "Death to spies".

video_title: Baby Touch & Feel Animals (perfectly designed for a baby's developmental stage) #toddlers #baby
description:
"Baby Touch & Feel: Animals" is a classic and fantastic choice for infant and toddler development. Here’s a detailed breakdown of what this book is, why it's so beneficial, and what to look for.

What is "Baby Touch & Feel: Animals"?
This book is part of the hugely popular DK Publishing "Baby Touch and Feel" series. It's a sturdy board book designed specifically for small hands.

The core concept is simple but brilliant: each page features a high-quality, vibrant photograph of a friendly-looking animal (like a kitten, puppy, or bunny) paired with a touch-and-feel element that mimics the animal's texture.

Key Features:

Board Book: Made of thick, laminated cardboard that can withstand chewing, drooling, and rough handling.

Real Photos: Uses clear, bright photographs instead of illustrations, which helps babies make a connection to the real world.

Textured Patches: Each animal has a patch of a different material to feel (e.g., fluffy chick, scratchy lion mane, smooth turtle shell, rubbery frog).

Simple Labels: The animal's name is printed in clear, large text.

Small Size: Perfect for little hands to hold and explore independently.

Developmental Benefits
This book is much more than just entertainment; it's a powerful learning tool.

Sensory Development: This is the primary benefit. The different textures (tactile sense) stimulate nerve connections in the brain, helping to build cognitive pathways.

Language & Vocabulary: As you read with your baby, you repeatedly say the animal's name and the sound it makes ("That's a fluffy lamb! Baa baa!"). This builds their early vocabulary.

Cognitive Skills: Babies learn cause and effect ("I touch this, and it feels different") and begin to categorize the world ("This is a dog, this is a cat").

Motor Skills: Turning the thick pages, patting the textures, and pointing at the pictures all help develop fine motor skills and hand-eye coordination.

Bonding: Snuggling up to read and explore the book together is a wonderful way to bond and provides a feeling of security for your baby.

What Age is it For?
The book is typically marketed for ages 0-3, but its use evolves as the child grows:

0-12 months: Primarily a sensory experience. They will grab, mouth, and pat the pages. You do most of the talking.

1-2 years: They start to recognize and point to animals on command ("Where is the dog?"), attempt to make animal sounds, and actively seek out their favorite textures.

2-3 years: They can name the animals themselves and describe the textures ("It's bumpy!" or "It's soft!").

Popular Titles in the Series
While "Animals" is the most classic, the series has expanded to include many themes. You might also see:

Baby Touch and Feel: Farm

Baby Touch and Feel: Bedtime

Baby Touch and Feel: Things That Go

Baby Touch and Feel: Words

Baby Touch and Feel: Meow! Meow! (or other sound-focused ones)

What to Look For & Considerations
Durability: These books are built to last, but the textured patches can occasionally come loose with very vigorous pulling. A little bit of child-safe glue easily fixes this.

Cleanability: The laminated pages can be wiped clean with a damp cloth, which is essential for baby books!

Alternatives: Other publishers (like Usborne and Priddy Books) have excellent touch-and-feel books. The "That's Not My..." series by Usborne is a particular favorite, using textures in a repetitive, language-building way ("That's not my puppy. Its ears are too fluffy!").

In summary, Baby Touch & Feel: Animals is an exceptional first book. It's engaging, educational, and perfectly designed for a baby's developmental stage. It's almost guaranteed to be a hit and a well-loved staple in your child's first library.

description:
Welcome spring with a book of sweet strawberries. There’s nothing like the sounds and smells of the first farmers market of the year. The sweetness of fresh fruits and local vegetables permeates the air and breathes new life into our recipes just as the spring brings new life to the earth. This illustrated tale follows the budding friendship between two girls who meet at their local farmers market and reminds us that food is the great unifier of all humankind.

When a farm family brings their spring crops to a city farmers market, the farmer’s daughter befriends the daughter of a neighborhood family doing their weekly shopping. Over the course of a year, the girls explore the bounty of each season. Sweet spring strawberries and crisp, fresh greens make way for corn on the cob, peppers, and a rainbow of tomatoes. Fall brings pumpkin patches and the crunch of apples. The friends part at the final winter market, already looking forward to the sweet red strawberries that will unite them again next spring.

description:
Keisha the Kind in My Little Sister Situation (Team Supercrew Series): A children's book about emotions, kindness, family, and sibling rivalry. 

Help your child to grow empathy, kindness, and compassion. Sibling rivalry? Keisha the Kind is here to help!

Meet Danny. He’s frustrated that he has to watch his little sister. He’s hungry for breakfast, she’s always getting into his things, and she wants to have a tea party. On top of all that, she gets all the attention! Team Supercrew’s Keisha the Kind comes to help when Danny needs it most. Ahoy Matey! It’s going to be a wild adventure.

Team Supercrew’s Keisha the Kind is here to remind kids that they have the power to be KIND inside of them whenever they need it!
Keisha the Kind is there to remind Danny that the worst-case fears in his mind are okay, and that he has the power to change these thoughts. Danny has the power to be KIND, and it just might be closer to find than he thinks.

Tools and tips for parents, teachers, and kids!
The Team Supercrew Book Series is rooted in cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), a social-emotional therapy that focuses on the ways that our thoughts, emotions, and behaviors are interconnected. Our thoughts create our feelings! When we develop the tools to change our negative thoughts, we learn how to regulate our emotions in a positive way.

Team Supercrew helps children recognize big feelings and have the tools to regulate emotions in a positive way!
The Team Supercrew heroes, Benny the Brave, Keisha the Kind, Chloe the Calm, and Gen the Grit, bring these tools to children and families in a fun, engaging, and unexpected way.

video_title: The Little Engine That Could (Self-Confidence)#educational #toddlers #kindergarten #kidsbooks #story
description:
"The Little Engine That Could" is a classic and beloved children's book that has inspired generations. Here’s a comprehensive overview.

The Story: A Summary
The story begins with a little train engine pulling a long line of cars filled with all sorts of wonderful things for the children on the other side of the mountain: toys, dolls, books, and delicious food.

Suddenly, the engine breaks down. The train is stuck. A shiny, full-sized passenger engine comes by, but when asked for help, it snobbishly refuses, stating it is too important for such menial work. Then a strong, big freight engine comes along, but it also refuses, claiming it is too tired.

Finally, a little blue engine (the protagonist of the story) approaches. She is not very big or very powerful, and she has never been over the mountain before. Seeing the sad faces of the toys and the desperate situation, she agrees to try.

As she starts the difficult climb up the steep mountain, she chugs to herself:

"I think I can—I think I can—I think I can."

This mantra gives her the strength and determination to keep going, even when the climb gets incredibly tough. Through sheer force of will and optimism, she successfully pulls the train over the mountain and down the other side to the waiting children.

As she goes down, she joyfully chugs to herself:

"I thought I could—I thought I could—I thought I could."

Key Themes and Why It's a Classic
Optimism and Positive Thinking: This is the core message. The story teaches that believing you can do something is the first and most important step to actually achieving it.

Perseverance and Hard Work: The little engine doesn't give up. She keeps trying, even when the task is difficult and she's small.

Kindness and Helping Others: The little engine helps not for a reward, but because it's the right thing to do. This contrasts with the selfishness of the other, bigger engines.

Self-Confidence: The story encourages children to believe in themselves, even when they feel small or incapable.

The book follows a class of students as they prepare and perform a play about the presidents of the United States. Today, Mike and his sister Pam are going on a shopping trip with Daddy. They all pile into the car and head downtown. First, they get haircuts. Mike hops into the chair, and then Pam. Next, they head over to the shoe store. A man measures Mike’s feet, and then he measures Pam’s. Mike picks out blue shoes. Pam is a copycat and picks out blue shoes as well.

The shoe store clerk gives them each a balloon, and Pam picks the same color as Mike. But on the way to the car, Pam’s balloon pops. Daddy gives Pam his balloon—and then decides to make an unexpected stop. Can you guess where they go?

Shopping with Daddy gives young readers a simple overview of a shopping trip—to the barber, a store, and a restaurant. Themes of sharing, copying, and mild sibling rivalry show up throughout the narrative. Written by Harriet Ziefert, illustrated by Travis Foster, and published by Blue Apple Books.

video_title: 🎃 Kids Book Read Aloud: GRUMPY PUMPKIN (How to deal with angry feelings) by Syperek and Izzy B
description:
It’s almost Halloween, Percival P. Pumpkin’s favorite time of year! But this year doesn't feel like the others, he has lost his smile, and doesn’t know why. Will he be able to learn to handle his angry feelings in a healthy way? Let's find out as we read together!

A cute, heartwarming, and inspirational story about a little pumpkin who is judged by his outward appearance rather than who he really is inside. With a lot of practice and help from a friend, he learns how to recognize, understand, and overcome his emotions. A wonderful message for all young children, and especially those dealing with social-emotional and self-acceptance. Teacher's Pick.

Author’s note: the authors, Michael and Lennon, are father and son. Lennon created the outline for the Grumpy Pumpkin as a first grader when the class was beginning to learn about descriptive writing. His dad wrote the story based on that outline. Now 9 years old and powered by ADHD and neurodivergent enabled, Lennon himself is a very social-emotional boy who receives behavioral development services to help him better understand his own feelings and emotions, as well as those of others.

Proceeds from sales of Grumpy Pumpkin will go to support children in need of such services as they have benefited Lennon greatly.

description:
If you are a parent of an absent-minded and anxious child, this book is a great way to introduce your little one to the concept of mindfulness. The story will suggest the ways to get rid of the distracting thoughts and will teach your child to stay focused and present.

Parents often struggle to explain their children how to deal with distraction, sorrow, and angry feelings. This mindfulness book for children is your best assistant to calm your children and to show kids’ exercises, which will help them to feel happy, focused, and calm.

When little Nick starts to miss everything that happens around him, his dad teaches him to deal with worries in a fun and playful way. By using kids' breathing techniques and other helpful tips, Nick learns to control his big feelings and becomes mindful.

This picture book is suitable for preschool kids as well as children ages 6-10, it contains lovely hand-drawn illustrations and charming rhymes. With an extra coloring page inside, this book will help your children:

to enjoy every moment and all the things surrounding them;
to use their senses and meditation in order to get rid of anxiety;
to share kindness and empathy towards others;
not to worry about things that haven't happened yet;
to use mindful kids’ activities in their daily life.

description:
Every parent must navigate the tricky situation of teaching kids about personal boundaries in a healthy, age-appropriate manner. Finding the right personal safety books to do it, however, just got easier with this book about personal space.

Little Nick’s story is a beautifully illustrated consent book for parents to read with their little boys and girls. In this boundaries for kids book, Little Nick experiences several situations that make him uncomfortable, but once he tells his parents, he gains new ways to address the situations.

What Kids Will Learn:

Body safety and awareness
Social skills
Consent for touch and no touch
Good touch, bad touch differentiation
Stranger danger
Little Nick’s story provides a great guide for social emotional learning for kids. All of the situations in the children’s safety books are relatable and useful for teaching consent to children in an age-appropriate manner, whether they’re a boy or girl.

The exceptional story lets kids see who their body belongs to, how to express their feelings in what’s said, what rules they might set up, and when there need to be exceptions to things like underpants for doctors.

This baby and child safety book is great conversation starter that kids can use while learning to read. The social emotional learning book for kids features rhyming text and high-quality illustrations that help children read the story themselves as they learn about good touch, bad touch for kids.

This body safety book for kids also promotes the basics for teaching kids about private parts. This kids’ book about safety increases body awareness for kids and is an excellent addition to any child’s library.

***

Body Boundaries Make Me Stronger is part of a series of social emotional books for kids that explore emotions, feelings, and social skills. This story is designed to help parents talk to their child about self-care, keeping safe, growing up, how to say what makes them uncomfortable, and much more.

video_title: Don't Push the Button! (playful, curiosity, temptation, & consequences) #kids #story #books #reading
description:
Theme: 
The central theme of Don’t Push the Button! is curiosity, temptation, and consequences. The book playfully explores how irresistible it can be to break rules, even when we know we shouldn’t.  

Summary: 
In this interactive children’s book by Bill Cotter, a little monster named Larry warns the reader *not* to push the big red button on the page… no matter what! But the temptation grows stronger as Larry makes silly excuses ("Unless you’re giving high-fives… then maybe?"), leading to hilarious chaos when the button is inevitably pressed. Each push triggers wild, colorful consequences (like multiplying Larrys or changing colors), requiring the reader’s help to fix the mess.  

Lesson: 
The story teaches kids about:  
1. Self-Control – Sometimes, rules exist for a reason, even if curiosity is strong.  
2. Problem-Solving – Mistakes happen, but we can take responsibility and find solutions.  
3. Fun & Engagement – The book turns a simple lesson into a joyful, interactive experience.  

Perfect for ages 3–7, it’s a humorous way to discuss impulse control while keeping kids giggling!

description:
“The Legend of Spookley the Square Pumpkin” is a heartwarming children’s book by Joe Troiano. Let me share the enchanting tale with you:

One day in the pumpkin patch, the strangest little pumpkin hatched. His name was Spookley, and he was different. While all the other pumpkins were round, Spookley was square! His unique shape made him stand out, and unfortunately, it also made him the target of teasing from the other pumpkins.

But Spookley had something special within him. When a stormy weather swept through the pumpkin patch just before Halloween, winds tossed the round pumpkins to and fro, crashing and bashing. Yet, Spookley remained steady—his square little body defying the chaos.

Could Spookley, with his unconventional shape, save the day? This delightful story delivers a powerful message of tolerance, kindness, and self-acceptance. It’s perfect for Halloween and every day of the year.

Transformation: New, smooth limbs sprouted from the gnarled stumps, symbolizing a visible demarcation between the tree’s past and present.
Living Reminder: Today, the Survivor Tree stands tall, a living testament to resilience, survival, and rebirth.
Seedling Program: Annually, the 9/11 Memorial shares seedlings from the Survivor Tree with three communities that have faced recent tragedies.

Confirmed in 1992, she served on the district court until 1998.
In 1997, nominated by President Bill Clinton to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit.
Eventually confirmed in 1998.

Taught at New York University School of Law and Columbia Law School.
President Barack Obama nominated her to the Supreme Court following the retirement of Justice David Souter.
