video_title: The Bee Who Lost Her Buzz (Self-Worth & Identity)#toddlers #kindergarten #kidsbooks #school #library
description:
The Bee Who Lost Her Buzz by Jennifer Waddle is a children's book with a clear and heartwarming theme that resonates with both children and adults.

The central theme of the book is:

Self-Worth and Identity Are Not Defined by a Single Ability or Trait.

This theme is developed through the story in several key ways:

1. The Crisis of Identity: The main character, Bumble, believes that her entire purpose and identity are tied to her ability to buzz. When she loses it, she feels useless and believes she is no longer a "real" bee. This mirrors the way people (especially children) can feel when they fail at something they believe is central to who they are.

2. The Value of Community and Teamwork: As Bumble seeks help from her friends—a butterfly, a cricket, and a ladybug—the story shows that everyone has unique strengths. The butterfly can fly high to look, the cricket can chirp to call for help, and the ladybug is a good listener. Bumble's value to the hive isn't just her buzz; it's her kindness and her role as a friend, which she maintained even when she had her buzz.

3. Inner Qualities Over External Talents: The resolution of the story emphasizes that Bumble's true strength was inside her all along. Her perseverance, courage, and willingness to ask for help are what ultimately save the day and, ironically, lead to the return of her buzz. The message is that character traits like kindness and determination are more fundamental to one's identity than any single skill.

4. It's Okay to Ask for Help: A secondary but important theme is that we don't have to solve our problems alone. Bumble’s journey shows that leaning on friends and community is a strength, not a weakness.

In essence, "The Bee Who Lost Her Buzz" uses a simple, relatable metaphor to teach that you are more than what you can do—you are who you are. Your value is inherent and not dependent on being perfect or always functioning at your best. It's a story about self-acceptance and discovering that our true "buzz" is the unique combination of heart, spirit, and community we bring to the world.

description:

This is a story about an assassination of a Civil Rights leader you might not know about.

Throughout the 1960s, a man named Edwin Pratt was the head of the Seattle Urban League, where he rallied against discrimination in hiring, education, and housing.

On a snowy night in 1969, three men carried out a hit on Pratt in his home, while his wife and five-year-old daughter Miriam were inside.

Miriam recently came to StoryCorps with her godmother Jean Soliz, who was her babysitter and neighbor at the time, to remember the aftermath.

“The Grouchy Ladybug” is a delightful children’s book by Eric Carle. Let’s explore the world of this irascible insect:

The Story: The Grouchy Ladybug is, well, quite grouchy! She wants to pick a fight with everyone she meets, regardless of their size. From a friendly ladybug to larger animals, she’s ready for a showdown.
Bullying and Consequences: This book humorously portrays the consequences of bullying. As the Grouchy Ladybug encounters various creatures, she learns valuable lessons about sharing, kindness, and manners.
Educational Concepts: As children follow her journey, they’ll grasp important concepts like time, size, and shape. Eric Carle’s bright artwork engages young readers.
Classic Appeal: For generations, this testy ladybug has delighted readers of all ages. Despite her grumpiness, she introduces us to new animals and discovers that being grouchy isn’t always the best option.
Recommended Age: Perfect for children aged 2 to 6 years, “The Grouchy Ladybug” is a timeless tale that combines humor, learning, and delightful illustrations.
So, let’s join the Grouchy Ladybug on her adventure and discover the power of kindness! 🐞

Ruby’s Mind: Ruby’s mind is always buzzing with ideas. One day, she stumbles upon some old boards and decides to build something remarkable.
Inviting Her Brothers: Ruby invites her brothers to help, but they dismiss her, laughing and claiming she doesn’t know how to build. Undeterred, Ruby declares, “Then I’ll learn!”
Dazzling Fort: Ruby’s determination pays off. She constructs a dazzling fort that captures everyone’s attention. Suddenly, her brothers want to play in it!
Last Laugh: Ruby, the little girl with big dreams, has the last laugh. Her creativity and persistence shine through, proving that she’s more than capable of building something extraordinary.

video_title: Say It With Me By Nancy S. Torres
description:
A story about a mother and child presented in both English and Spanish that affirms how radiant and wonderful we all are.


In Say It With Me (Dilo conmigo), a heartwarming dual-language picture book for children ages 4-8, a child repeats their mama’s inspiring messages and makes her words their own.

Following words written by Ecuadorian-American elementary school educator and meditation guide Nancy S. Torres and set to gorgeous illustrations by Zoey Black, young readers will learn the power of speaking kindly about themselves and how good it feels to share a love for yourself with others.

The Perfect Gift for Grownups, New Parents, and Little Ones Alike

From their smile, to their skin, to their beautiful brains, Say It With Me (Dilo conmigo) teaches young readers and their grownups how to recognize what makes them remarkable — and the significance of being the person who helps them see.

Gift this book to a loved one (or yourself) and start a brand new and loving ritual that will be passed down for generations.

Pika gathers grass to store for the colder days.
Blue Thrush takes flight and heads south to escape the chill.
Brown Bear settles in for a long, cozy nap.
But what about yaks? What do they do when the snow arrives? Little Yak wonders.

In the end, as the flurries begin to fall, Mother Yak tells Little Yak to “snuggle close.” And that’s when Little Yak discovers the secret: While other animals sleep, hide, or go away, yaks get to see the beautiful snow.

Jonathan Allen’s illustrations bring the snow to life, making it seem like it’s dancing across the pages. The wide-eyed expressions of the animals add to the charm of the story.

video_title: Shante' Keys and the New Year's Peas #kids #story #books #learning #reading #readaloud #newyear
description:
Shante' Keys and the New Year's Peas by Gail Piernas-Davenport is a delightful children's book that explores themes of cultural diversity, family traditions, and the importance of sharing and learning about others' customs. Here's a breakdown of the theme, summary, and lesson of the story:

Theme
The central theme of the book is cultural awareness and inclusivity. It highlights how different families celebrate New Year's with unique traditions, emphasizing the value of understanding and respecting diverse customs.

Summary
The story follows Shante' Keys, a young girl who is excited to celebrate New Year's Day with her family. Her grandmother prepares a traditional meal of black-eyed peas, collard greens, and cornbread, which are believed to bring good luck and prosperity in African American culture. However, when Shante' discovers they are out of black-eyed peas, she embarks on a journey through her neighborhood to borrow some.

As she visits her neighbors, Shante' learns about the different ways they celebrate the New Year. For example:

Mrs. Garcia celebrates with a Mexican tradition of eating 12 grapes at midnight.

Mr. Lee shares his Chinese New Year customs, including red envelopes and dragon dances.

Ms. Patel explains her Indian New Year celebration, which involves lighting lamps and sharing sweets.

By the end of the story, Shante' not only finds the black-eyed peas but also gains a deeper appreciation for the diverse traditions of her community. She returns home to enjoy her family's meal, enriched by the knowledge she has gained.

Lesson
The story teaches children the importance of celebrating diversity and being open to learning about others' traditions. It encourages curiosity, respect, and inclusivity, showing that while people may have different ways of celebrating, these differences make the world a richer and more interesting place. Additionally, it highlights the value of family traditions and the joy of sharing them with others.

This book is a wonderful resource for teaching children about cultural diversity and the significance of New Year's traditions around the world. It’s perfect for sparking conversations about inclusivity and the beauty of different cultures.

This book by Laura Numeroff, illustrated by Felicia Bond is perfect for beginning readers and storytime!
It’s a great circular tale: If you give a mouse a cookie, he's going to ask for a glass of milk.
 When you give him the milk, he'll probably ask you for a straw.
 When he's finished, he'll ask you for a napkin.
Then he'll want to look in a mirror to make sure he doesn't have a milk mustache. After that, he will be thirsty and asking for milk and sure a cookie matches the milk.

description:
Life often feels like an endless wave of struggles — but what if peace was always within us? 🌊

This powerful parable story, “How to Stop Suffering in Life,” follows Daniel, a hardworking man from a coastal town who spends his life searching for happiness outside himself. When he meets an old sailor named Mr. Gray, he learns a profound truth that changes his entire perspective — that suffering ends not when life gets easier, but when we stop resisting what is.

Through beautiful storytelling and emotional depth, this story will remind you that peace doesn’t come from control — it comes from acceptance, awareness, and inner stillness.

✨ Watch till the end to understand how Daniel’s heart transforms, and learn the timeless lesson that can help you find peace in your own life.

📘 Moral of the Story:

You can’t stop the waves, but you can learn to stay calm within them. True peace begins when we stop fighting with life.

video_title: The Very Greedy Bee (Consequences of Actions/Redemption) #toddlers #kindergarten #school #teacher
description:
"The Very Greedy Bee" is a popular and charming children's picture book written by Steve Smallman and illustrated by Jack Tickle.

Here is a summary and analysis of the book:

Summary
The story follows a little bee who is, as the title suggests, very greedy. On a beautiful sunny day, instead of collecting pollen and nectar to take back to the hive like all the other bees, he chooses to keep it all for himself.

The Feast: He finds a beautiful meadow full of flowers and drinks all the nectar from the petals, one flower at a time. He gorges himself so much that he becomes too fat and sleepy to fly.

The Consequence: He falls asleep in the last flower he emptied. When he wakes up, it is night time, and all the other flowers have closed for the evening. He is all alone, stranded, and still very hungry. He realizes he has no way to get home and no food for the night.

The Rescue: Just as he begins to cry, some friendly insects he had previously ignored and shooed away—including a moth, some ants, and a firefly—come to his aid. The firefly lights the way, and the other insects help push and guide him back to his hive.

The Lesson: Grateful for their kindness, the bee learns his lesson. The next day, he not only collects nectar for the hive but also finds a special, juicy flower which he shares with his new friends as a thank you.

Key Themes
Greed vs. Sharing: This is the central theme of the book. The bee's greed leaves him isolated and in trouble, while sharing and cooperation solve his problems and lead to friendship.

Consequences of Actions: The story clearly shows that selfish actions have natural consequences. The bee's greed directly leads to him being stranded and hungry.

Kindness and Friendship: Despite the bee's earlier selfishness, the other insects show him compassion and help him without asking for anything in return. This act of kindness teaches him the value of community and friends.

Redemption: The bee is given a chance to make up for his mistake. He learns from his error and changes his behavior, becoming a better member of his community.

Why It's a Great Children's Book
Engaging Story: The narrative is simple, sequential, and easy for young children to follow.

Vivid Illustrations: Jack Tickle's artwork is bright, colorful, and expressive, perfectly capturing the lush meadow and the bee's changing emotions.

Clear Moral: The lesson is presented in a non-preachy, natural way that children can easily understand through the bee's experience.

Interactive Elements: The book often includes "slurping" and "burping" sounds, which make it fun for read-aloud sessions.

Relatable Scenario: The concept of not wanting to share is something many young children struggle with, making the bee's journey and lesson highly relatable.

In essence, "The Very Greedy Bee" is a delightful tale that uses a relatable insect character to teach young readers about the importance of sharing, kindness, and the value of friendship in a fun and engaging way.

description:
“The Cat in the Hat” is a beloved children’s book written and illustrated by the iconic American author Theodor Geisel, who is better known by his pen name, Dr. Seuss. Let’s dive into the whimsical world of this classic tale:

Title: The Cat in the Hat
Genre: Children’s literature
Language: English
Illustrator: Dr. Seuss
Publisher: Random House, Houghton Mifflin

The story revolves around a tall, mischievous, and anthropomorphic cat who sports a distinctive red and white-striped top hat and a jaunty red bow tie. One rainy day, the Cat unexpectedly appears at the home of siblings Sally and her brother. Their mother is away, leaving them in the care of their skeptical pet fish.

Despite the fish’s repeated objections, the Cat proceeds to entertain the children with a series of whimsical tricks. Alongside the Cat are his mischievous companions, Thing One and Thing Two. However, their antics lead to chaos, and they end up wreaking havoc in the house.

As the children and the fish grow increasingly alarmed, the Cat unveils a magical cleaning machine that tidies up the mess just in time—disappearing right before their mother returns home.

Geisel wrote “The Cat in the Hat” in response to concerns about early childhood literacy and the limitations of traditional primers. The book’s success was immediate, captivating both critics and young readers. Within three years of its debut, it had already sold over a million copies. In 2001, it ranked as the ninth best-selling children’s book of all time according to Publishers Weekly.

This delightful tale not only revolutionized early reading but also introduced the iconic Cat himself—a character who would become synonymous with Dr. Seuss’s legacy. The Cat’s mischievous spirit lives on, enchanting generations of readers and inspiring adaptations, including a 1971 animated television special and a 2003 live-action film.

So, whether you’re revisiting this classic or discovering it for the first time, “The Cat in the Hat” promises a whimsical adventure that transcends generations! (AI generated).

“Thomas & Friends: Journey Beyond Sodor” is a captivating animated musical adventure film and feature-length special based on the beloved British television series Thomas & Friends. This delightful tale draws inspiration from The Railway Series by Wilbert Awdry.

Henry’s Accident: Henry, while delivering a goods train to the Mainland, faces an accident due to a faulty signal. His derailment prompts Thomas to step up.
Thomas Takes Charge: Upset that Sir Topham Hatt has chosen James to replace Henry, Thomas decides to collect the goods train himself. But the Troublesome Trucks lead him astray.
Uncharted Territory: Thomas encounters a gantry crane named Beresford and two experimental engines, Theo and Lexi. Their unique personalities add excitement to his journey.
Steelworks Mystery: Thomas stumbles upon a massive Steelworks factory run by two enigmatic engines: Hurricane and Frankie. They invite him to stay, but things take an unexpected turn.
Friendship and Escape: Thomas learns that Hurricane delivered his train to Bridlington overnight. Frankie convinces him to help at the Steelworks, but they refuse to let him leave. Thomas escapes, meeting a third experimental engine named Merlin.
James Joins the Quest: Back on Sodor, James grows fed up with Thomas’ absence and sets out to find him. His journey leads him to the Steelworks.
Rescue Mission: Thomas enlists the help of the experimental engines to rescue James, and together, they face challenges and discover the true meaning of friendship.
This heartwarming film introduces themes of courage, empathy, and acceptance. It’s a must-watch for young fans of Thomas and his adventurous world! 🚂🌟(AI generated).

video_title: Railroad Hanks (Problem-Solving & Teamwork/Humor) #educational #toddlers #kindergarten #kidsbooks
description:
"Railroad Hank" is a delightful and quirky children's book by Lisa Moser, with illustrations by Benji Davies. It's a favorite for its gentle humor, heartwarming message, and charming characters.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the book, perfect for a parent, teacher, or librarian.

Railroad Hank
Author: Lisa Moser

Illustrator: Benji Davies

Recommended Age Range: 3-7 years old

Plot Summary
Railroad Hank is a well-meaning but rather literal-minded train engineer who chugs up the mountain on his little red train. He hears that his friend Granny Brett is feeling "unsalubrious" (a fancy word for unwell). Hank decides he must cheer her up immediately!

His solution? To bring her a "gift that will make her smile."

Along the winding track, he asks various friends for advice:

Missy May suggests he bring Granny some eggs for scrambling.

Cinnamon Cobbler suggests bringing bacon to sizzle with the eggs.

Hank Plank suggests bread for toast.

Rebo the Rake suggests tomatoes for a nice, red slice.

But Hank takes every suggestion a little too literally. Instead of collecting the items, he tries to bring the entire source of the items to Granny Brett:

He doesn't take a few eggs; he loads the entire henhouse onto his train!

He doesn't take a side of bacon; he brings the whole pig!

He doesn't take a loaf of bread; he brings the field of wheat!

He doesn't take a tomato; he brings the entire tomato plant!

His train becomes a hilarious, clattering, chaotic mess of animals and plants by the time he reaches the top of the mountain. When he arrives, Granny Brett is indeed confused by the bizarre gifts. But with the help of all their friends, they use Hank's gifts to make a wonderful community breakfast. Granny Brett isn't "unsalubrious" anymore; she's cheered up by the silly gesture and the time spent with everyone she loves.

Key Themes
Miscommunication & Literal Thinking: The core of the book's humor is Hank's innocent and literal interpretation of language. This is very relatable for young children who are still learning the nuances of words and phrases.

The Thought That Counts: Hank's gifts are impractical, but his heart is 100% in the right place. The story beautifully shows that genuine care and effort are more important than getting the details perfect.

Community & Helping Others: Everyone on the mountain comes together to help a friend in need (Granny Brett) and to help another friend who is trying to help (Hank).

Problem-Solving & Teamwork: The "problem" of the chaotic gifts is solved when everyone works together to turn them into a delicious meal.

Why Kids Love It
The Silliness: A train carrying a pig, a henhouse, and a field of wheat is just objectively funny.

Repetition & Predictability: The pattern of Hank stopping, getting advice, and misinterpreting it allows kids to anticipate the joke and feel "in on it."

The Illustrations: Benji Davies's artwork is warm, expressive, and filled with funny details that kids love to spot (like the increasingly distressed expressions of the animals on the train).

The Happy Ending: A joyful community feast is a satisfying and positive conclusion.

Why Parents & Educators Love It
Rich Vocabulary: Introduces fun words like "unsalubrious," "scramble," "sizzle," and "relish."

Teaching Opportunity: It's a great springboard for discussions about idioms, figurative language, and how words can have multiple meanings.

Social-Emotional Learning (SEL): Teaches empathy (cheering up a friend), kindness, and the value of community.

Engaging Read-Aloud: The repetitive structure and opportunities for different character voices ("Chug-a-chug-a-chug!") make it a fantastic book for reading aloud.

Activities & Discussion Questions
After reading, you can extend the fun with:

What would you bring? If your friend was sad, what would you bring to cheer them up? (This helps move from literal to thoughtful gifts).

Act it out: Kids can love pretending to be the train, chugging around and picking up increasingly silly items.

Draw your own train: What other silly things could Railroad Hank have put on his train? Draw a picture of an even crazier train car.

video_title: The Magical Yet (Embrace Challenges, Persistence) #kids #toddlers #kindergarten #story #educational
description:
The Magical Yet is a charming and inspirational rhyming picture book, beautifully illustrated by Lorena Alvarez Gómez. It is designed to help children develop a growth mindset and understand that it's okay not to be able to do something... yet.

Overview and Theme
The central character is a young child who faces various challenges and frustrations—things they can't do, like riding a bike without training wheels, tying their shoes, or doing a cartwheel. Instead of framing these as failures, the book introduces a concept: the "Yet."

The "Yet" is portrayed as a magical, friendly creature that follows the child everywhere. It represents the power of potential, practice, and perseverance. The core message is that with time, effort, and a positive attitude, the skills that seem impossible now will eventually be mastered.

Key Messages
Growth Mindset: The book is a direct and accessible lesson in having a growth mindset (the idea that abilities can be developed through dedication and hard work) versus a fixed mindset (the idea that abilities are innate and unchangeable).

Embrace Challenges: It encourages children to see challenges not as roadblocks, but as exciting opportunities to learn and grow.

Persistence: It normalizes struggle and teaches that it's a necessary part of the learning process. The repeated phrase "You can't do it yet" is empowering.

Self-Compassion: It helps kids be kinder to themselves when they don't get something right on the first try.

Target Audience
The book is perfect for:

Children ages 4-8 who are encountering new and difficult tasks.

Parents and educators looking for a tool to encourage resilience and a positive attitude toward learning.

Anyone who needs a reminder that it's never too late to learn something new.

The Illustrations
Lorena Alvarez Gómez's illustrations are vibrant, whimsical, and full of energy. The "Yet" itself is depicted as a glowing, starry, magical being that changes form, sometimes looking like a helpful companion and other times like a spark of inspiration. The visuals perfectly capture the feeling of frustration transforming into triumphant joy.

Why It's So Popular
Relatable: Every child (and adult) has faced something they find difficult.

Hopeful and Uplifting: It turns a moment of defeat into a promise of future success.

Beautifully Crafted: The rhyming text is catchy and easy to read aloud, making it a great bedtime or classroom story.

In essence, The Magical Yet is more than just a book; it's a concept that gives children a powerful word to add to their vocabulary. It provides a framework for resilience that they can carry with them long after the story is over. It’s a modern classic in the genre of social-emotional learning for children.

description:
Martin Luther King, Jr. was a remarkable leader in the American civil rights movement. His tireless efforts and powerful speeches played a pivotal role in advocating for racial equality, justice, and peace. Here are some key points about him:

Early Life and Education:
Born on January 15, 1929, in Atlanta, Georgia, Martin Luther King Jr. grew up in a religious household.
He excelled academically and attended Morehouse College, where he studied sociology and theology.
Later, he pursued his doctorate in systematic theology at Boston University.
Civil Rights Activism:
Dr. King became a prominent figure in the fight against racial segregation and discrimination.
He led the Montgomery Bus Boycott in 1955 after Rosa Parks was arrested for refusing to give up her seat to a white person on a bus.
His leadership in the Southern Christian Leadership Conference (SCLC) further fueled the civil rights movement.
I Have a Dream Speech:
One of Dr. King’s most iconic moments was his “I Have a Dream” speech delivered during the 1963 March on Washington.
In this powerful address, he called for an end to racial segregation and envisioned a future of equality and harmony.
Nonviolent Resistance:
Dr. King believed in nonviolent protest as a means to effect change.
He organized sit-ins, marches, and boycotts to challenge discriminatory laws and practices.
Legacy and Impact:
Martin Luther King Jr. received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964 for his commitment to nonviolence and justice.
His tragic assassination on April 4, 1968, shocked the world but solidified his legacy.
His work continues to inspire generations, emphasizing the importance of love, compassion, and equality.
Remember, Dr. King’s vision of a more just and equitable society remains relevant today. Let us honor his memory by promoting understanding, empathy, and unity. (AI generated).

video_title: A Poor Excuse for a Dragon. Read Aloud Kids Books
description:
Fred the dragon has a list of tasks he must complete in order to be a successful dragon—none of which comes naturally. But he's determined to make #5—eat people—work. Before you can say "pass the salt" he's gobbled up three people even though he doesn't have the stomach for it. Luckily a local shepherd, with the help of a giant and a witch, knows how to cure what ails him and get those pesky people out of his belly. It's happily-ever-after for everyone in ways you'd never expect.

Geisel award-winning author/illustrator Geoffrey Hayes is a stepped reader maestro. The common threads between his wildly popular Uncle Tooth and Otto SIRs and the more recent Benny and Penny series (Toon Books) are clear and constant. The art is adorable, the characters are bursting with personality, and the stories are humorously subversive. From marauding pirates to misbehaving mice to a dragon who swallows people whole (and then continues to communicate with them in his belly!), Geoffrey always hits that sweet spot for the stepped reader audience—easy to decode, illustrative tales that tickle the funny bone.

*Tangled* is a humorous and whimsical children's poem about a group of farm animals that accidentally get their body parts tangled together—tails, wings, legs, and more—causing chaos and confusion. As they struggle to free themselves, the situation becomes increasingly absurd, with the animals hilariously knotted in a big mess.  **Theme:**

The playful tone suggests that even in confusing situations, patience and teamwork can lead to a solution.

description:
Goodnight Tractor is a delightful bedtime book for little ones who adore farms, tractors, and all things that go. Written by Michelle Robinson and illustrated by Nick East, this charming book will help ease your child into a gentle sleep. Let’s explore the world of tractors and farm animals as we say goodnight:

“Goodnight farmer.”
“Goodnight plow.”
“Goodnight trailer.”
“Goodnight cow.”
“Goodnight dog, and goodnight sheep…”
“Goodnight Tractor, time to sleep.”
The soothing rhymes and relaxing illustrations make it perfect for:

Tractor and truck-loving boys and girls
John Deere fans
Babies and toddlers aged 1-3 who adore farms and farm animal stories
If your little one enjoys classics like Goodnight Moon and Goodnight, Goodnight Construction Site, they’ll surely love Goodnight Tractor too!

Dan, the Taxi Man is a delightful picture book written by Eric Ode and illustrated by Kent Culotta. Let’s hop into the backseat of Dan’s taxi and explore this musical adventure:

“Here’s Dan, Beep! Beep! the Taxi Man, going to the show and picking up the band.”
Climb inside while you still can with Dan, Beep! Beep! the Taxi Man."
And what a band it is! A symphony of sounds and colors, this cumulative tale is as much fun to read aloud as it is to listen to. Let’s meet the band members:

Maureen with her tambourine
Tyrone with his saxophone
Star with her electric guitar
Claire with a rattly snare
Ace with his upright bass
With each new passenger, the rhymes are playfully repeated: “Climb inside while you still can with Dan, Beep! Beep! the Taxi Man.” The font styles and sizes generate appropriate instrument noises from readers, adding to the excitement:

Star’s “Whee, wazzle, wah”
Tyrone’s “Squeeba-dee dee”
And, of course, Dan’s ever-honking horn!
The brightly colored, energetic illustrations by Kent Culotta bring this mod-inspired tale to life. Imagine mohawk hair, dreads, an afro, and Dan’s red handlebar mustache – it’s a rockin’ good time!

Dan, the Taxi Man is perfect for little musicians, future drivers, or any 2-to-5-year-old who loves fun books. So find this book, put it on the shelf, but don’t expect it to stay there long – your child will want re-reads, often! (AI generated).

The passing of a pet can be an emotional challenge for both kids and adults. For many, losing a pet feels like losing a beloved member of the family — and we all grieve in our own ways.

Children may not understand where the array of feelings they are experiencing come from, or are going. And that's okay.

video_title: The World Works Better Read Aloud by Reading Pioneers Academy
description:
We all want the world to work better, but what can we do to help that happen?
As children and as adults, we often feel the desire to improve our lives and the world we live in... but we don't always know how to turn those desires into actions. Sometimes, we don't even know how to express the changes we'd like to create.

This children's nonfiction book, with space-themed illustrations and simple statements about what makes the world work better, provides many simple starting-points for conversation and for action -- opening up topics such as:
Kindness
Support
Positivity
Responsibility
Justice
Thoughtfulness

Teach your children the story that we all implicitly understand, but all too often forget: the story of all the things they already know about how to make our world work better:
Each page in this book finishes a sentence about what makes the world work better, but the end of each sentence is the beginning of a journey... because the story isn't inside this book. The story is inside YOU.
So use this book to spark ideas and inspire meaningful conversations with yourself, with your children, or even with your team at work.
And keep it as a reminder that all the adventure, discovery, and limitless potential of childhood are yours to enjoy -- at any age.

video_title: Saving American Beach - Read Aloud With Author Heidi Tyline King | Brightly Storytime Together
description:
This heartfelt picture book biography tells the story of MaVynee Betsch, an African American opera singer turned environmentalist and the legacy she preserved. Get the book: https://bit.ly/3yQQftA

ABOUT THE BOOK:

MaVynee loved going to the beach. But in the days of Jim Crow, she couldn’t just go to any beach–most of the beaches in Jacksonville were for whites only. Knowing something must be done, her grandfather bought a beach that African American families could enjoy without being reminded they were second class citizens; he called it American Beach. Artists like Zora Neale Hurston and Ray Charles vacationed on its sunny shores. It’s here that MaVynee was first inspired to sing, propelling her to later become a widely acclaimed opera singer who routinely performed on an international stage. But her first love would always be American Beach.

After the Civil Rights Act desegregated public places, there was no longer a need for a place like American Beach and it slowly fell into disrepair. MaVynee remembered the importance of American Beach to her family and so many others, so determined to preserve this integral piece of American history, she began her second act as an activist and conservationist, ultimately saving the place that had always felt most like home

description:
“Thidwick the Big-Hearted Moose” is a charming children’s book written by the legendary Dr. Seuss. First published in 1948, this delightful tale takes us on an adventure with Thidwick, a moose with a heart as big as the forest.

Here’s a glimpse into the story:

Thidwick, a moose living on the northern shore of Lake Winna-Bango, is part of a herd that thrives on moose-moss. One day, a small bug politely asks to ride on Thidwick’s antlers (which are mistakenly referred to as horns in the book). Being kind-hearted, Thidwick agrees, allowing the bug to hitch a free ride.

But things take an unexpected turn. The bug invites other animals to join the moose’s antlers—a woodpecker, a spider, and more. Thidwick, ever the gracious host, treats them as “guests,” even though he never explicitly granted them permission to live there.

As the animal entourage grows, so does the chaos. When the woodpecker starts drilling holes in Thidwick’s antlers, the other moose give him an ultimatum: either get rid of the freeloaders or leave the herd. Thidwick’s sense of decency leads him to choose his guests over herd life, and he remains behind.

Winter arrives, and the herd swims across the lake for fresh moose-moss. Thidwick wants to follow, but his guests object—they consider his antlers their home. Starvation looms, yet Thidwick remains steadfast, honoring their wishes.

Meanwhile, the ungrateful residents on his antlers invite even more animals, including a hefty black bear. Hunters spot Thidwick, aiming to mount his head as a trophy. Desperate, he remembers it’s time to shed his antlers. Just before capture, he drops them, escapes, and rejoins his herd.

His former guests, however, meet a different fate—they’re stuffed and mounted on the trophy wall of the Harvard Club. Thidwick’s story explores the limits of hospitality, selflessness, and the consequences of being too big-hearted. (AI generated).

While young children are avid observers and questioners of their world, adults often shut down or postpone conversations on complicated topics because it's hard to know where to begin. description:
"I'd Know You Anywhere, My Love" is a beautiful and reassuring children's picture book written and illustrated by the acclaimed Nancy Tillman.

Here's a detailed breakdown of the book:

Overview
Author/Illustrator: Nancy Tillman

Genre: Children's Picture Book (Ages 1-4)

Themes: Unconditional love, parental love, imagination, reassurance, identity.

Style: Lyrical, rhyming text with lush, dreamlike, and whimsical illustrations.

Plot Summary
The book doesn't have a traditional narrative plot. Instead, it presents a series of whimsical and imaginative scenarios where a child is transformed into various animals or creatures.

A loving parent (the narrator) assures the child that no matter what disguise they take on—whether a bear in a cave, a rhino, a snake, an octopus, or even a monster—their love is so powerful and their connection so strong that they would always be able to recognize them.

The core message is one of unwavering, unconditional recognition and love.

Key Themes and Messages
Unconditional Love: The central theme is that a parent's love is constant and sure, regardless of how a child might look or act.

Reassurance and Security: It comforts children with the idea that they are always known and loved, providing a deep sense of security.

Imagination: The book celebrates a child's imagination, playfully exploring the idea of transformation and pretend.

The Bond Between Parent and Child: It beautifully captures the unique and intuitive connection a parent has with their child.

Illustrations
Nancy Tillman's illustrations are a hallmark of her work. For this book, they are:

Ethereal and Magical: Featuring soft, glowing colors and dreamy landscapes.

Whimsical: The animals are realistic yet placed in fanciful situations (e.g., a rhino wearing a gold crown).

Full of Love: The images are warm and tender, perfectly complementing the text's message.

Detailed: Children love to look at the pictures and find small details, like the hidden hearts Tillman often includes.

Sample Text (Rhyming)
The book is written in a gentle, rhyming cadence. A typical passage goes:

"If you were a mother bear sleeping deep in your den,
I'd know you anywhere, my love, and I'd find you again.
If you were a rhino, charging out of the trees,
I would know your great horn, and I'd get down on my knees..."

Why Parents and Children Love It
Perfect for Bedtime: The soothing rhythm and reassuring message make it an ideal bedtime story.

Interactive: Parents often point to the different animals and ask, "Is that you?" which children enjoy.

Beautiful Artwork: The illustrations are captivating for both adults and children.

Emotional Resonance: It perfectly puts into words and pictures the profound love a parent feels for their child.

Comparison to Other Books
It is very much in the style of Nancy Tillman's other bestselling books, such as "On the Night You Were Born," which shares a similar theme of a child's unique and celebrated place in the world.

The theme of unconditional love places it alongside classics like "Guess How Much I Love You" by Sam McBratney or "Love You Forever" by Robert Munsch, though Tillman's style is distinctly more magical and illustrative.

In summary, "I'd Know You Anywhere, My Love" is a heartfelt, gorgeously illustrated promise of love and recognition that has become a beloved favorite on many children's bookshelves. It's a wonderful gift for new parents, toddlers, and anyone who wants to share a message of unwavering love with a child.

video_title: 1 hr+ Camping Story Picture Books #kids #toddlers #kindergarten #education #story #reading #books
description:
A camping trip is an adventure that reconnects you with nature, simplifies life, and creates lasting memories. Whether you're a first-timer or a seasoned pro, there's always something new to learn.

I. Types of Camping
First, decide what style of camping suits you best:

Car Camping: Your vehicle is parked right at your campsite. 

Backpacking: You carry everything you need on your back to hike to remote, often primitive, sites. It's about minimalism and self-sufficiency.

RV / Van Camping: Camping with a home on wheels. 

Glamping ("Glamorous Camping"): For those who love the idea of nature but not sacrificing luxury.

Dispersed / Wild Camping: Camping for free on public lands outside of designated campgrounds. 

Canoe/Kayak Camping: Paddling to your campsite, which is often on a remote shoreline.

II. Essential Gear (The "Big 5")
Your shelter, sleep system, and pack are the most critical pieces.

Shelter:

Tent: Choose a size rated for one more person than you have (a 3-person tent for 2 people).

Alternatives: Hammock with rainfly & bug net, bivy sack, or tarp.

Sleep System:

Sleeping Bag: Rated for temperatures colder than you expect. Down is lighter and more packable; synthetic insulates better when wet.

Sleeping Pad: Provides insulation from the cold ground and comfort. Options include inflatable, self-inflating, or closed-cell foam.

Backpack:

For backpacking, a properly fitted pack is crucial. 

For car camping, any durable bag or tub will work for transporting gear.

Lighting:

Headlamp: Hands-free is essential for cooking, setting up tent in dark, or reading. Always bring extra batteries.

Lantern: For ambient light at the campsite (propane, battery, or solar).

Cooking System:

Stove: Portable propane canister stoves are easy for car camping. 

Fuel: Bring more than you think you'll need.

Cookware: A simple pot/pan set, spatula, and mug/bowl.

Cooler: For car camping, a high-quality cooler is key for keeping food fresh.

III. Clothing: The Layering System
Dress in synthetic or wool layers to manage moisture and temperature. Avoid cotton (like jeans and hoodies).

Base Layer: Moisture-wicking (Merino wool or synthetic).

Mid Layer: Insulation (fleece, down, or synthetic puffy jacket).

Outer Layer (Shell): Waterproof and windproof rain jacket and pants.

Extras: Beanie, gloves, extra socks (wool is best!), and sturdy footwear (hiking boots or trail runners).

IV. Food & Water
Water: Plan for 2 liters per person per day (more for hiking). Have a way to treat water from natural sources: filter, purification tablets, or boiling.

Food: Keep it simple!

Easy Meals: Oatmeal (breakfast), sandwiches & snacks (lunch), dehydrated meals, pasta, or hot dogs (dinner).

Snacks: Trail mix, jerky, energy bars, and dried fruit are great fuel for hiking.

The "Camp Kitchen Box": Pack salt/pepper, oil, utensils, a sharp knife, a sponge, and biodegradable soap.

V. Planning & Preparation
Choose a Destination & Campsite: Research parks (National, State, private). Use sites like Recreation.gov to reserve spots early, especially on weekends.

Check the Weather: Be prepared for it to change suddenly.

Plan Your Meals: Make a menu so you pack exactly what you need.

Learn the Rules: Know the check-in/out times, fire regulations (are there burn bans?), and wildlife protocols.

Tell Someone Your Plans: Leave your itinerary and expected return time with someone not on the trip.

VI. Campfire Basics
Check for Fire Bans: Always the first step.

Use Existing Rings: If one is available, use it.

Keep it Small: A manageable fire is a safe fire.

Fuel: Only burn local, dead firewood. Never transport firewood long distances as it can spread invasive insects.

VII. Leave No Trace Principles
This is the ethical code for enjoying the outdoors responsibly.

Plan Ahead and Prepare.

Travel and Camp on Durable Surfaces (established trails and sites).

Dispose of Waste Properly (Pack it in, Pack it out). This includes all trash and food scraps.

Leave What You Find (don't pick flowers or take rocks).

Minimize Campfire Impacts.

Respect Wildlife (observe from a distance, never feed animals).

Be Considerate of Other Visitors.

video_title: Swing! A Scanimation Picture Book (brilliantly engineered book) #educational #toddlers #kindergarten
description:
"Swing!: A Scanimation Picture Book" is a delightful and innovative children's book that never fails to captivate both kids and adults.

Here is a detailed overview of the book.

Swing!: A Scanimation Picture Book
Author: Rufus Butler Seder
Genre: Children's Picture Book, Interactive, Novelty
First Published: 2008

What is "Swing!"?
"Swing!" is the flagship title in the popular Scanimation series by Rufus Butler Seder. It's not a traditional storybook but rather a visual experience that uses a groundbreaking technology to create the illusion of movement on the page.

The Magic of Scanimation Technology
The book's entire concept revolves around its patented Scanimation design. Each page is made up of two layers:

The illustrated background: This contains the static parts of the image (e.g., a field, a sky, a pond).

A transparent plastic sheet: Overlaid on the illustration is a sheet with black vertical bars.

As the reader moves the book (or moves their head slightly while looking at it), the bars pass over a series of sequential images printed beneath them. This tricks the eye and brain into perceiving fluid, continuous motion—much like a vintage zoetrope or the earliest forms of animation.

The effect is pure magic. The animals and people on the page genuinely appear to run, jump, swim, and swing right before your eyes.

Content and Structure
The book is simple, rhythmic, and designed for very young readers.

Rhyming Text: Each page features a short, energetic rhyme that describes the action:

"You swing on the swings. / You slide down the slide."

"A horse runs. / A frog jumps."

"An eagle soars. / A dinosaur roars!"
The text is large, clear, and perfect for read-aloud sessions.

Vibrant Illustrations: The color palette is bright and engaging, using bold colors that appeal to children. The moving subjects are often depicted in a sepia-toned or high-contrast style to make the animation effect as clear as possible.

The Actions: The book showcases a variety of motions that children can easily recognize and often mimic themselves, making it highly interactive. Examples include:

A girl swinging

A boy sliding

A horse galloping

An eagle flying

A basketball player dunking

A dinosaur roaring

Target Audience
Age Range: Perfect for toddlers and preschoolers (ages 1-4). Its durability (board book format) makes it able to withstand rough handling from little hands.

Appeal: It is a huge hit with children who are kinesthetic learners and anyone who loves cause-and-effect. It's also a fantastic book for reluctant readers, as the "wow factor" of the animation draws them in.

Why Kids (and Parents) Love It
Interactive and Engaging: Kids don't just sit and listen; they actively move the book, tilt it, and marvel at the results. It turns reading into a physical activity.

High "Wow" Factor: The illusion of motion is incredibly effective and feels like real magic to a young child. The first reaction is almost always a gasp or a giggle of delight.

Educational Value: It teaches verbs (action words) in the most memorable way possible. Children see the word "run" while literally watching a horse run.

Durable Construction: As a sturdy board book, it's built to last through many readings and explorations.

Timeless Appeal: While technology advances, the simple, analog cleverness of Scanimation remains impressive and charming.

The Scanimation Series
"Swing!" was the first and most famous book, but its success led to a whole series, including:

Gallop! (Featuring animals)

Waddle! (Featuring penguins and birds)

Kick! (Featuring sports actions)

Star Wars: A Scanimation Book

And many more seasonal and thematic titles

In summary, "Swing!" is a modern classic of children's publishing. It’s a brilliantly engineered book that transforms reading into an active, magical experience, fostering a lifelong love of books through the timeless wonder of movement and animation. It's a guaranteed crowd-pleaser and a wonderful gift for any young child.

video_title: Fred And Ted Go Camping (a book full of opposites! a great way to introduce antonyms!)#kindergarten
description:
Fred and Ted Go Camping is a classic Beginner Book from the beloved children's series by Peter Eastman, son of the legendary P.D. Eastman (Go, Dog. Go!).

Here is a summary and overview of the book.

Fred and Ted Go Camping
Author: Peter Eastman
Series: Part of the "Fred and Ted" series, which also includes Fred and Ted Like to Fly and Fred and Ted's Road Trip.

Summary
The story follows two dog friends, Fred (a tall, lanky yellow dog) and Ted (a short, stout blue dog), who are polar opposites in how they do things, but the best of friends.

They decide to go on a camping trip together. The entire book humorously contrasts their different approaches to every task:

Packing: Fred packs light and neatly, while Ted packs an enormous, comical pile of gear.

Traveling: Fred has a small, compact car, while Ted has a huge, clunky car. They take different routes but end up at the campsite at the same time.

Setting Up Camp: Fred easily sets up a small, simple tent. Ted struggles with a large, complex tent that eventually collapses on him.

Fishing: Fred catches a tiny fish with a simple pole. Ted, with elaborate gear, catches a giant fish that pulls him into the lake.

Cooking: Fred cooks his small fish over a small, controlled fire. Ted tries to cook his giant fish over a huge, out-of-control bonfire.

Sleeping: Fred is cozy in his small tent. Ted is tangled in the canvas of his collapsed tent.

The Storm: A rainstorm arrives. Fred's tent is watertight, while Ted's is not. Ted ends up taking shelter in his car, which he has packed so full he can't lie down to sleep.

Going Home: The next morning, they decide to head home. True to form, Fred easily packs up, while Ted's attempt to pack is a messy disaster. They finally drive off together in Ted's car, with Fred's little car hitched to the top.

Despite their mishaps, they both enjoy their trip and remain happy companions.

Themes and Why It's a Classic
Celebration of Differences: The core message is that friends can have completely different styles and personalities and still have a wonderful time together. Their differences are what make the story fun.

Simple Humor: The visual gags and the stark contrast between the two characters are hilarious and easily understood by young children.

Basic Vocabulary: As a Beginner Book, it uses simple, repetitive language perfect for early readers (e.g., "Fred had a little car. Ted had a big car.").

Engaging Illustrations: The clean, colorful illustrations are essential to the storytelling, often telling the joke without needing any words.

It's a charming, funny, and wholesome book that has been a favorite for generations, teaching a gentle lesson about friendship and acceptance through laughter.

video_title: Never,  Not Ever! (a young, stubborn bat named Pascaline who is about to start school) #kids #story
description:
"Never, Not Ever" by Beatrice Alemagna is a beloved and critically acclaimed picture book that has captured the hearts of children and adults alike.

Here is a detailed overview of the book.

Overview
Title: Never, Not Ever
Author/Illustrator: Beatrice Alemagna
Original Title: Mai, mai, mai, non ci andrò! (Italian, 2015)
English Translation: Published in 2016 by Thames & Hudson
Target Age: 3-7 years old

The Story
The plot is a simple yet profoundly relatable childhood dilemma. The story follows a young, stubborn bat named Pascaline who is about to start school.

On the big day, instead of getting ready, Pascaline announces to her large family (consisting of mom, dad, and what seems like hundreds of brothers and sisters) her firm decision:

"Never, not ever will I go to school!"

To emphasize her point, she uses a powerful magic word she knows: "CATASTROPHISOCK!" This word is so mighty that it makes her shrink to the size of a berry.

Now tiny, she hitches a ride in her mother's bag, believing she has successfully avoided school. Unbeknownst to her, her mother is on her way to... Pascaline's school.

Pascaline arrives in the classroom, hidden in the bag. She observes the new environment from her secret vantage point and slowly, her perspective begins to change. She sees other children who are also a little unsure, a kind teacher, and interesting things to do. Her fear and stubbornness melt away as curiosity takes over. Eventually, she pops out of the bag, grows back to her normal size, and joyfully joins her new class, completely forgetting her earlier vow.

Themes
First Day Jitters: The book perfectly captures the anxiety and resistance many children feel about starting something new, like school.

The Power of Perspective: Pascaline's change of heart comes from observing the situation safely from a distance. Once she sees it isn't scary, she's willing to participate.

Curiosity Overcoming Fear: The story shows how natural curiosity can be a more powerful force than fear.

Independence and Growth: Pascaline makes the decision to join the class all by herself, which is a huge step toward independence.

Artistic Style and Illustrations
Beatrice Alemagna's illustrations are the heart and soul of the book. They are instantly recognizable and deeply expressive.

Mixed Media: She uses a combination of gouache, collage, pencil, and oil pastels, creating rich, textured, and visually engaging pages.

Expressive Characters: Pascaline's emotions are vividly portrayed through her large, round eyes and small body language—from defiant pouts to wide-eyed wonder.

Color Palette: The colors are warm, earthy, and slightly muted, creating a cozy and comforting atmosphere, even in moments of frustration.

Charming Details: The pages are filled with delightful details, from the quirky outfits of Pascaline's enormous bat family to the busy, creative chaos of the classroom.

Why It's So Highly Regarded
Relatable for Children: It validates their fears without ever being preachy. It doesn't tell children why they should go to school; it shows them why they might end up wanting to.

Empowering Resolution: The solution doesn't come from parents forcing the child. Pascaline's change of heart is internal and organic, making it a truly empowering story.

Unique Protagonist: A bat is a unusual and charming choice for a school story, making it stand out.

Artistic Excellence: It is considered a masterpiece of picture book illustration, winning over critics, librarians, and educators for its unique and beautiful style.

Awards and Recognition
Winner of the 2016 Pépite d'Or (Golden Egg) for best picture book at the Montreuil Children's Book Fair in France.

A New York Times Best Illustrated Children's Book of 2016.

A Washington Post Best Children's Book of 2016.

Widely praised by major review publications including Publishers Weekly, School Library Journal, and Booklist.

In summary, "Never, Not Ever" is a warm, witty, and visually stunning picture book that tackles a universal childhood experience with immense empathy, humor, and artistic brilliance. It's a modern classic and a perfect read for any child nervous about a new beginning.

video_title: The Most Magnificent Thing. Read Aloud Kids Books
description:
An unnamed girl and her very best friend, who happens to be a dog. The girl has a wonderful idea. "She is going to make the most MAGNIFICENT thing! She knows just how it will look. She knows just how it will work. All she has to do is make it, and she makes things all the time. Easy-peasy!" But making her magnificent thing is anything but easy, and the girl tries and fails, repeatedly. Eventually, the girl gets really, really mad. She is so mad, in fact, that she quits. But after her dog convinces her to take a walk, she comes back to her project with renewed enthusiasm and manages to get it just right. For the early grades' exploration of character education, this funny book offers a perfect example of the rewards of perseverance and creativity. The girl's frustration and anger are vividly depicted in the detailed art, and the story offers good options for dealing honestly with these feelings, while at the same time reassuring children that it's okay to make mistakes. The clever use of verbs in groups of threes is both fun and functional, offering opportunities for wonderful vocabulary enrichment. The girl doesn't just "make" her magnificent thing -- she "tinkers and hammers and measures," she "smoothes and wrenches and fiddles," she "twists and tweaks and fastens." These precise action words are likely to fire up the imaginations of youngsters eager to create their own inventions and is a great tie-in to learning about Science, Technology, Engineering and Math.

video_title: Don't Eat the Bees Don't Eat the Bees (Life Lessons from Chip the Dog) #toddlers #kindergarten #kids
description:
"Don't Eat the Bees" by Dev Petty, illustrated by Mike Boldt.

At a Glance
Title: Don't Eat the Bees (Life Lessons from Chip the Dog)

Author: Dev Petty

Illustrator: Mike Boldt

Genre: Children's Picture Book (Ages 3-7)

Publisher: Crown Books for Young Readers

Publication Date: May 23, 2023

The Story
The book is narrated by Chip, a proud and cheerful dog who believes he has life all figured out. He sees it as his duty to bestow his wisdom upon the reader (and any nearby humans), and his number one, most important rule is: "DON'T EAT THE BEES."

Chip explains this rule with the absolute certainty of a dog who has, in fact, learned this lesson the hard way. He enthusiastically lists all the wonderful, delicious things a dog should eat, such as:

Shoes

Homework

Cat poop

Pizza (found under a couch)

In contrast, he emphatically explains why bees are a very, very bad choice. His reasoning is a hilarious mix of dog logic and painful experience—they are "spicy," they "buzz angry," and they make your face puffy.

The humor builds as Chip's "advice" continues, revealing that while he understands the bee rule perfectly, his judgment on other edible items is... highly questionable.

Themes and Why It's Loved
Humor: This is the book's biggest strength. The contrast between the one very sensible rule and Chip's otherwise terrible ideas is incredibly funny for both children and adults.

Relatable Dog Behavior: Any dog owner will recognize the truth in Chip's personality. The book perfectly captures a dog's single-track mind, their confusion about some things, and their bizarre dietary choices.

Simple, Clear Message: For kids, the core message is simple and memorable: don't eat bees! It's a great, silly way to teach a small but important lesson about safety (without being preachy).

Engaging Narration: Chip speaks directly to the reader, making the story feel personal and interactive.

The Illustrations
Mike Boldt's artwork is vibrant, expressive, and perfectly matches the comic tone of the text. Chip is depicted as an adorable, clueless bulldog with a wildly expressive face. The illustrations brilliantly show the consequences of his actions (like a comically swollen muzzle after a bee encounter) and the chaos he creates while pursuing his other "approved" snacks.

Overall Impression
"Don't Eat the Bees" is a riotously funny and charming picture book. It's a fantastic read-aloud choice that will have kids giggling and repeating Chip's signature line. It's in the same vein as Dev Petty and Mike Boldt's other successful collaborations like I Don't Want to Be a Frog, using a stubborn but lovable animal character to deliver a big dose of humor.

It's highly recommended for:

Young children who love silly stories.

Dog lovers.

Parents and teachers looking for an engaging and funny read-aloud book.

In short, Chip the dog is a hilarious guide to life, and his most important lesson is one you won't forget: no matter how tempting it might be... DON'T EAT THE BEES!

About ARELI IS A DREAMER

In the first picture book written by a DACA Dreamer, Areli Morales tells her own powerful and vibrant immigration story.

When Areli was just a baby, her mama and papa moved from Mexico to New York with her brother, Alex, to make a better life for the family–and when she was in kindergarten, they sent for her, too.
 
Everything in New York was different. Gone were the Saturdays at Abuela’s house, filled with cousins and sunshine. Instead, things were busy and fast and noisy. Areli’s limited English came out wrong, and schoolmates accused her of being illegal. But with time, America became her home. And she saw it as a land of opportunity, where millions of immigrants who came before her paved their own paths. She knew she would, too.
 
This is a moving story–one that resonates with millions of immigrants who make up the fabric of our country–about one girl living in two worlds, a girl whose DACA application was eventually approved and who is now living her American dream.
 
The Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) is an immigration policy that has provided relief to thousands of undocumented children, referred to as “Dreamers,” who came to the United States as children and call this country home.
